domains.title: Magnetism: fields, quantum matter and controlled inference
domains.summary: A source-linked hierarchy from classical currents and magnetic energy to quantum materials, spin transport, superconducting screening and reproducible magnetometry.
domains.scope: Selected foundations and2024–2026 primary/preprint evidence. Not an exhaustive literature survey, patentability opinion, material certification or hardware demonstration. Abstract-only papers and unreviewed branches remain explicitly marked.

topics.title: Magnetism: fields, matter and controlled inference
topics.summary: A multiscale map from current-generated fields to quantum materials, spin transport and calibrated measurement. Physical mechanisms and evidence status remain separate.

topics.title: Classical magnetic fields
topics.summary: Currents, flux continuity, potentials and boundary-value problems.

topics.title: Induction and electromagnetic energy
topics.summary: Time-dependent fields, motional circuits, local energy transfer and passive device budgets.

topics.title: Magnetic order and material response
topics.summary: Response functions and microscopic interactions connect atomic moments to domains and phases.

topics.title: Low-dimensional and moiré magnets
topics.summary: Dimensionality, anisotropy, stacking and correlations control order and textures.

topics.title: Spin transport and magnetic dynamics
topics.summary: Angular momentum transfer, resonances, textures and wave-based information processing.

topics.title: Superconducting magnetic response
topics.summary: Equilibrium flux exclusion, screening currents, vortices and critical scales.

topics.title: Magnetoelectric and hybrid systems
topics.summary: Cross responses need conjugate variables, symmetry and an external energy supply.

topics.title: Magnetometry and inverse inference
topics.summary: Measurements require channel models, geometry, calibration and identifiable source parameters.

topics.title: Computational magnetism
topics.summary: Discretization, energy functionals, verification, uncertainty and reproducibility.

topics.title: Flux density and field intensity
topics.summary: B describes magnetic induction; H separates free current from macroscopic magnetization. Neither can be replaced by the other without a constitutive statement.

topics.title: Current distributions
topics.summary: Line, surface and volume current idealizations have different supports and units.

topics.title: Steady current kernels
topics.summary: Magnetostatics assumes stationary sources with consistent return currents.

topics.title: Biot–Savart reconstruction
topics.summary: The vector kernel weights each source element by orientation and distance; near-wire singularities reveal the idealization.

topics.title: Straight-wire symmetry
topics.summary: An infinitely long thin wire permits a closed-form azimuthal field; finite leads break that symmetry.

topics.title: Current-loop geometry
topics.summary: Axial loop fields provide a controlled route from a finite circuit to the far-field dipole.

topics.title: Ampèrian integral methods
topics.summary: An integral law is always valid in its domain but solves a field only when symmetry controls the integrand.

topics.title: Solenoids and return flux
topics.summary: Long-coil interior estimates omit fringe fields and winding resistance.

topics.title: Vector potential and gauge
topics.summary: A curl representation enforces flux continuity; gauge choice does not change B.

topics.title: Magnetic dipoles and force
topics.summary: Dipole approximations require source-target separation large relative to source extent.

topics.title: Bound versus free current
topics.summary: Magnetization produces volume curl and surface cross-product currents; classifications depend on material coarse graining.

topics.title: Interface boundary conditions
topics.summary: Normal B continuity and tangential H jumps encode flux conservation and free surface current.

topics.title: Faraday induction
topics.summary: Changing flux and moving material circuits contribute to the same oriented emf.

topics.title: Motional electromagnetic circuits
topics.summary: The velocity in a circuit emf is the velocity of the material boundary, not a guessed wave velocity.

topics.title: Displacement current
topics.summary: A changing electric displacement repairs continuity and enables waves; quasistatics needs a scale argument.

topics.title: Local energy accounting
topics.summary: Poynting flux, storage and mechanical/Joule work identify where supplied energy goes.

topics.title: Passive ports and finite time
topics.summary: Initial stored energy and all powered auxiliary ports belong in a finite-window budget.

topics.title: Hysteretic losses
topics.summary: A loop measures cycle work only for declared field variables, sample volume and measurement conditions.

topics.title: Eddy currents and skin effect
topics.summary: Diffusion and conductive loss can shift response peaks without adding an energy source.

topics.title: Macroscopic susceptibility
topics.summary: A scalar constant susceptibility is a restricted linear, reversible approximation.

topics.title: Demagnetizing fields
topics.summary: Applied and internal fields differ; ellipsoids supply a special uniform-field solution.

topics.title: Thermal paramagnetism
topics.summary: Independent moments give a high-temperature weak-field Curie law, not a universal low-temperature law.

topics.title: Microscopic exchange
topics.summary: An effective spin Hamiltonian represents electronic exchange after model reduction.

topics.title: Ordered phases
topics.summary: An order parameter and symmetry specify a phase more precisely than the presence of a magnetic signal.

topics.title: Ferromagnetism
topics.summary: Parallel order can form domains that hide a large local moment behind small net magnetization.

topics.title: Domains and walls
topics.summary: Exchange, anisotropy and magnetostatics compete to set walls and domain patterns.

topics.title: Continuum wall profiles
topics.summary: A one-dimensional wall width follows from a specific functional and boundary states.

topics.title: Antiferromagnetism
topics.summary: Opposing sublattice moments require a Néel order parameter, not just net M.

topics.title: Ferrimagnetism and compensation
topics.summary: Unequal sublattices can compensate net magnetization or angular momentum at different temperatures.

topics.title: Frustrated interactions
topics.summary: Not all preferred pairwise alignments can be simultaneously realized on a frustrated lattice.

topics.title: Quantum spin liquids
topics.summary: Absence of conventional order alone is insufficient; competing states and disorder must be tested.

topics.title: Altermagnetic symmetry
topics.summary: Some compensated collinear orders allow momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting.

topics.title: Material-specific RuO2 controversy
topics.summary: Bulk magnetic order, thin-film structure, spin/orbital conversion and interfacial effects are separate claims.

topics.title: Criticality and finite-size scaling
topics.summary: Apparent transitions in finite systems require size, dimensionality and dynamical-time analysis.

topics.title: Two-dimensional order
topics.summary: Continuous spin symmetry and short-range interactions restrict finite-temperature order; anisotropy changes the premises.

topics.title: van der Waals layers
topics.summary: Weak interlayer bonding permits assembly but does not make exchange or disorder negligible.

topics.title: Twist and stacking
topics.summary: Twist changes local registry and therefore exchange, anisotropy and relaxation.

topics.title: Moiré supercell phase coexistence
topics.summary: Spatially separated local phases and transition scales need resolved measurement rather than one averaged moment.

topics.title: Electrostatic tuning of magnets
topics.summary: A gate can alter carriers, electric field and strain; these mechanisms must be discriminated.

topics.title: Spin–valley correlations
topics.summary: Valley labels are electronic momentum-space degrees of freedom, not real-space locations.

topics.title: Magnetic parent states and pairing
topics.summary: Field-enhanced superconductivity and valley imbalance constrain mechanisms without proving one unique pairing theory.

topics.title: Magnetization dynamics
topics.summary: The sign convention for gyromagnetic ratio and choice of B or H must be explicit.

topics.title: Ferromagnetic resonance
topics.summary: A resonance depends on effective-field curvature, damping, geometry and drive/readout channels.

topics.title: Magnonics
topics.summary: Spin waves carry energy and angular momentum; excitation, propagation and detection losses remain.

topics.title: Exchange-dominated dispersion
topics.summary: A quadratic wavevector term is a limiting continuum result, not every film mode dispersion.

topics.title: Spin and orbital transport
topics.summary: Spin, orbital and charge currents have distinct units and conversion mechanisms.

topics.title: Spin Hall conversion
topics.summary: A conversion angle is defined only after specifying current normalization and geometry.

topics.title: Spin–orbit torque switching
topics.summary: Coherent torque, heating and field-induced switching require separate controls.

topics.title: Chiral textures
topics.summary: DMI, exchange, anisotropy and dipolar energy stabilize or destabilize different textures.

topics.title: Skyrmions and topological charge
topics.summary: A continuum integer invariant requires smoothness and a compactified or fixed boundary.

topics.title: Optical writing of magnetic textures
topics.summary: Laser pulses are an external energy input; field-free is not energy-free.

topics.title: Ultrafast Néel dynamics
topics.summary: Two-sublattice exchange gives dynamics not captured by a single ferromagnetic macrospin.

topics.title: Meissner equilibrium response
topics.summary: Equilibrium flux expulsion differs from frozen flux in an ideal perfect conductor.

topics.title: London screening
topics.summary: A local homogeneous superfluid model gives exponential screening only in a stated geometry.

topics.title: Fluxoid and phase winding
topics.summary: Phase single-valuedness constrains a fluxoid; magnetic flux alone needs additional limits.

topics.title: Type-II vortices
topics.summary: Vortex cores, penetration depth and sample geometry distinguish lower and upper critical fields.

topics.title: Ginzburg–Landau description
topics.summary: A coarse-grained order parameter has a controlled near-transition regime, not unrestricted microscopic authority.

topics.title: Magnet–superconductor hybrids
topics.summary: Stray fields, screening, proximity and dissipation couple distinct subsystems.

topics.title: Cross-response thermodynamics
topics.summary: A derivative with respect to H differs by permeability factors from one with respect to B.

topics.title: Linear magnetoelectric tensor
topics.summary: Symmetry and chosen thermodynamic potential determine allowed reciprocal cross responses.

topics.title: Layer-resolved orbital response
topics.summary: A bilayer layer-pseudospin response is not automatically the bulk SI magnetoelectric coefficient.

topics.title: Magnetoelastic transduction
topics.summary: Changing strain can modify anisotropy; external electrical/mechanical work remains in the budget.

topics.title: Cavity and resonator hybrids
topics.summary: Avoided crossing alone does not establish a useful autonomous energy source or quantum advantage.

topics.title: Sensor transfer functions
topics.summary: A magnetometer produces a calibrated channel with finite bandwidth, orientation and noise.

topics.title: NV-center magnetometry
topics.summary: Zeeman shifts depend on the projection along a known crystallographic axis and the applicable spin Hamiltonian.

topics.title: Hall and inductive probes
topics.summary: Hall voltage and pickup-coil emf measure different functions of the same field history.

topics.title: Measurement uncertainty
topics.summary: Calibration, correlation, geometry and drift can dominate counting noise.

topics.title: Inverse magnetization
topics.summary: External fields need not uniquely determine a vector magnetization distribution.

topics.title: Height continuation and bandwidth
topics.summary: High-spatial-frequency components decay rapidly above the sample and amplify noise on inversion.

topics.title: Magnetic inverse null spaces
topics.summary: A single field component generally cannot identify every source component without extra assumptions.

topics.title: Physics-informed reconstruction
topics.summary: A fitted field can coexist with multiple magnetization explanations; priors and held-out data must be reported.

topics.title: Micromagnetic energy functionals
topics.summary: A continuous unit-vector model excludes atomic-scale degrees of freedom by construction.

topics.title: Mesh and timestep convergence
topics.summary: Agreement at one grid spacing is not convergence; resolve relevant exchange and wall scales.

topics.title: Exchange functional
topics.summary: Gradient penalties approximate slowly varying exchange and need compatible boundary conditions.

topics.title: Anisotropy functional
topics.summary: Easy axes and energy offsets must be stated with the coefficient convention.

topics.title: DMI conventions and boundaries
topics.summary: Bulk and interfacial DMI have different invariant forms and boundary twists.

topics.title: Code verification versus validation
topics.summary: Analytic/standard-problem agreement verifies implementation within a model, not actual material parameters.

topics.title: MuMax3 verification corpus
topics.summary: Selected source sections expose finite-difference approximations and even benchmark disagreement.

topics.title: Electronic-structure model choices
topics.summary: Exchange-correlation approximations and Hubbard U can change predicted magnetic ground states.

topics.title: Reproducibility and uncertainty
topics.summary: Record code/version, mesh, convergence, material parameters, boundary conditions and numerical budgets.

formulas.title: Magnetic flux continuity
formulas.plain: Divergence-free B has zero net outward flux through a closed surface.
conditions: Classical Maxwell theory with no magnetic monopoles; include all faces of a closed surface.
derivation: Apply the divergence theorem to local flux continuity.
Opposite face contributions cancel for a uniform field.

steps: Top flux=+0.0001 Wb; bottom=-0.0001 Wb; sides zero.

limitingCases: A nonzero open-surface flux is entirely compatible.
pitfalls: Zero divergence does not imply zero curl or zero local field.

formulas.title: Biot–Savart law for a filament
formulas.latex: \mathbf B(\mathbf r)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int \frac{d\boldsymbol\ell\times(\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime)}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime|^3}
formulas.plain: Sum oriented steady-current elements using the inverse-distance vector kernel.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
oriented line element in current direction

conditions: Steady localized current with a physically completed return path; vacuum.
Observation point is outside the ideal filament.
derivation: Solve the vector Poisson equation in Coulomb gauge with the free-space Green function.
Take its curl to obtain the cross-product kernel.

workedExample.inputs: Circular loop I=1 A, R=0.1 m; evaluate centre
steps: All axial contributions add; transverse contributions cancel.
Integrate circumference to obtain mu0 I/(2R).

limitingCases: The far field of a localized closed loop is dipolar, not an isolated-wire 1/r field.
pitfalls: Do not omit return current when predicting a finite device field.

formulas.title: Infinite straight wire
formulas.plain: Cylindrical symmetry turns Ampere circulation into an azimuthal field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Infinite thin wire, vacuum, stationary current; r exceeds conductor radius.
derivation: Choose a coaxial circular contour.
B is tangential and constant on the contour, so 2 pi r B=mu0 I.
limitingCases: As I tends to zero, B vanishes; the singular r→0 limit is outside the thin-wire domain.
pitfalls: A finite wire cannot inherit this expression arbitrarily close to its ends.

formulas.title: On-axis circular-loop field
formulas.plain: The axial field of a thin circular loop interpolates between centre field and a dipole.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Circular filament in vacuum; observation on its symmetry axis.
derivation: Project the Biot–Savart cross product onto the axis.
The denominator is constant around the loop; integrate azimuth.
limitingCases: At z=0 recover mu0 I/(2R); for |z|≫R recover z^-3.
pitfalls: The expression is not the off-axis field of a finite solenoid.

formulas.title: Magnetostatic free-current circulation
formulas.plain: H circulation counts free current after magnetization is separated out.
conditions: Stationary fields; displacement current negligible; contour and normal follow right-hand orientation.
derivation: Apply Stokes theorem to curl H=Jf.
Integrate current density over the spanning surface.

workedExample.inputs: Ienc=3 A; circular contour radius=0.1 m with cylindrical symmetry

limitingCases: Zero enclosed current gives zero circulation, not necessarily H=0 everywhere.
pitfalls: Ampere law does not justify constant H on a nonsymmetric contour.

formulas.title: Long-solenoid interior estimate
formulas.plain: Turns per unit length set the ideal long air-core coil field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Length much larger than radius, observation away from ends, air core, negligible winding thickness.
derivation: Choose an Ampere rectangle along the interior and remote exterior.
Neglect exterior contribution and count n*l turns.
limitingCases: At an ideal long coil end the on-axis field is about half the deep-interior value.
pitfalls: Real coil heating, fringe fields and magnetic core saturation are separate calculations.

formulas.title: Macroscopic B–H–M relation
formulas.plain: Magnetization is magnetic moment per material volume; the relation defines H in SI.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Macroscopic SI fields defined at compatible coarse-graining scale.
derivation: Separate microscopic current into free and magnetization contributions.
Define H=B/mu0−M; no linear material law is assumed.

workedExample.inputs: Collinear H=100 A/m and M=900 A/m

limitingCases: For M=0, vacuum B=mu0 H; at H=0 an ordered sample can have M≠0.
pitfalls: B and H do not have the same SI units; B=mu H additionally assumes a constitutive law.

formulas.title: Volume magnetization current
formulas.plain: Spatially varying magnetization has an equivalent bound volume current.
conditions: Continuum magnetization differentiable inside the material; add interface surface currents separately.
derivation: Represent localized magnetic moments as small current loops.
Interior loop contributions cancel except where magnetization varies.
limitingCases: Uniform M has zero volume curl but generally nonzero surface current.
pitfalls: Zero Jb in the bulk does not imply an unmagnetized body.

formulas.title: Surface magnetization current
formulas.plain: The boundary current closes magnetization loops at an interface.
conditions: Use the magnetization jump if both sides are magnetic; orientation is outward from the chosen body.
derivation: Integrate volume curl through an infinitesimal interface layer.
The normal derivative of the magnetization step produces a surface sheet.
limitingCases: A face normal parallel to M carries no equivalent surface current.
pitfalls: The order M cross n matters; reversing it reverses circulation.

formulas.title: Far-field magnetic dipole
formulas.latex: \mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r^3}[3(\mathbf m\cdot\hat{\mathbf r})\hat{\mathbf r}-\mathbf m]
formulas.plain: A localized current distribution has a leading magnetic dipole term.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: r much larger than source extent; outside the source in vacuum.
derivation: Expand the localized vector potential at large distance.
The closed-current monopole term vanishes; curl the leading moment term.

workedExample.inputs: m=0.1 A m²; axial r=0.1 m

limitingCases: At the equator the field points opposite m with half the axial magnitude.
pitfalls: The singular point-dipole field cannot describe the source interior.

formulas.title: Dipole torque and energy
formulas.plain: A fixed permanent dipole tends to align with the applied field.
conditions: Small fixed moment in a field uniform over the dipole; induced moments require material work accounting.
derivation: Sum Lorentz forces around a small loop.
Integrate torque against angle to obtain U=−mB cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: m=0.01 A m²; B=0.1 T; perpendicular orientation
workedExample.result: Torque=0.001 N m; aligned U=−0.001 J

limitingCases: Aligned torque is zero although energy is minimal, not zero by necessity.
pitfalls: An induced moment may introduce a factor1/2 in energy after its formation is included.

formulas.title: Force on a fixed dipole
formulas.plain: The gradient of dipole potential gives force when its moment is fixed.
conditions: Small rigid moment, quasistatic external field, derivatives at fixed m.
derivation: Use F=−gradient U with U=−m dot B.
Keep self field and induced-response work outside this simplified potential.

steps: Multiply mz by axial field gradient.

limitingCases: A uniform field can exert torque but gives no translational dipole force.
pitfalls: A field magnitude alone is insufficient to determine lifting force.

formulas.title: Magnetic flux
formulas.plain: Flux is the oriented surface integral, not B multiplied by any convenient area.

variables.meaning: magnetic flux through chosen oriented surface

conditions: A defined surface and normal; B and geometry may vary across it.
derivation: Sum infinitesimal normal field contributions.
For a uniform field and flat area, obtain BA cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: B=0.2 T; A=0.01 m²; field at60degrees to normal

limitingCases: A surface parallel to field has zero flux despite nonzero B.
pitfalls: Angle is measured from the normal, not from the surface plane.

formulas.title: Oriented moving-loop Faraday law
formulas.plain: Electric and motional contributions give the emf around the actual moving material loop.
conditions: A well-defined material circuit and right-hand orientation; ideal thin circuit approximation.
derivation: Combine local curl E=−partial B/partial t with the moving-surface transport theorem.
The boundary motion term is v cross B, not an extra energy source.

workedExample.inputs: Stationary loop, flux rises by0.003 Wb over0.1 s
workedExample.result: emf=−0.03 V for the chosen positive circulation

limitingCases: Steady B can induce emf if the loop area/orientation changes.
pitfalls: Reversing the chosen normal reverses both flux and emf sign consistently.

formulas.title: Ampère–Maxwell law
formulas.plain: Free current and displacement-current density both source the curl of H.
conditions: Macroscopic Maxwell equations with polarization placed in D.
derivation: Add displacement current to preserve free-charge continuity.
Taking divergence gives divergence Jf+partial rho_f/partial t=0 using divergence D=rho_f.

workedExample.inputs: Charging capacitor: dD/dt=2 A/m² over0.01 m²
steps: Integrate displacement current density over gap area.

limitingCases: The term may be negligible in a specific MQS limit, not identically absent.
pitfalls: Displacement current is not a flow of free charges across an ideal vacuum capacitor gap.

formulas.title: Vacuum Poynting theorem
formulas.latex: \partial_t u+\nabla\cdot\mathbf S=-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf E,\quad\mathbf S=\mathbf E\times\mathbf H
formulas.plain: Field storage plus outward electromagnetic flux equals negative work rate on matter.
conditions: Vacuum fields with material currents treated explicitly; material storage needs a consistent constitutive energy model.
derivation: Dot Ampère–Maxwell with E and Faraday with H.
Subtract using divergence(E cross H)=H dot curl E−E dot curl H.

workedExample.inputs: Control volume: inward flux3 W; stored-energy rise1 W
steps: Outward integrated S=−3 W; dU/dt=1 W.

limitingCases: A steady state can have nonzero energy flux while storage is constant.
pitfalls: Field enhancement is not net output; include every boundary port and initial storage.

formulas.title: Vacuum field-energy density
formulas.plain: Quadratic vacuum storage follows from reversible field work.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Vacuum or a specified linear nondispersive analogue; not a general hysteretic-material formula.
derivation: Integrate E dD and H dB along a reversible constitutive path.
In vacuum D=epsilon0 E and H=B/mu0.

workedExample.inputs: E=0; B=0.01 T in volume0.001 m³

limitingCases: Storage vanishes quadratically as B→0.
pitfalls: Using B²/(2mu) in a nonlinear hysteretic core can give incorrect material energy accounting.

formulas.title: Passive inductor and winding budget
formulas.plain: Source power splits into changing magnetic storage and nonnegative winding dissipation.
conditions: L positive and constant, R≥0, no additional coupled or powered ports.
derivation: Multiply voltage equation by current.
Use L i di/dt=d(Li²/2)/dt.

workedExample.inputs: L=0.1 H; i rises0→2 A; R=0 for illustrative storage
workedExample.result: Input work=0.2 J; no continuous output from a fixed stored state

limitingCases: With source off, a resistor can drain initial energy but cannot replenish it.
pitfalls: A changing L introduces mechanical/coupling work; do not omit it.

formulas.title: Cycle work in magnetic material
formulas.plain: An oriented quasistatic B–H loop gives magnetic work per sample volume for a completed cycle.

variables.meaning: net supplied work per cycle per volume

conditions: Closed periodic cycle, consistent internal field and sample volume; separate nonmagnetic apparatus losses.
derivation: Integrate local magnetic work H dot dB.
Reversible storage returns to its initial value after a cycle, leaving net dissipative work.

workedExample.inputs: Rectangular scalar loop: coercive Hc=100 A/m; remanent Br=0.5 T
workedExample.result: Dissipated work=200 J/m³ per cycle under this loop idealization

limitingCases: A reversible single-valued path traversed forward and back encloses zero area.
pitfalls: A counterclockwise plotted loop may change algebraic sign; passivity uses work supplied to matter.

formulas.title: Ellipsoidal internal-field correction
formulas.plain: A uniform ellipsoid gives a closed correction for reversible scalar susceptibility.
conditions: Uniform ellipsoid, principal-axis drive, linear reversible medium; SI factors sum to1.
derivation: Combine demagnetizing field −NM with M=chi Hint.
Solve the one-variable linear equation for M.
limitingCases: For chi→0, M≈chi Happ; large chi is shape-limited.
pitfalls: CGS demagnetizing factors can sum to4pi; do not mix conventions.

formulas.title: Weak-field Curie susceptibility
formulas.plain: Independent isotropically orientable moments respond linearly when thermal energy dominates alignment.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Noninteracting moments in weak field mu B≪kB T; classical orientation or appropriate quantum effective moment.
derivation: For classical isotropic independent moments use x=mu B/(kB T) and Z_orientation=4pi sinh(x)/x. Its mean axial moment is mu[coth(x)−1/x].
Expand coth(x)−1/x=x/3+O(x³), multiply by number density, and use B≈mu0 H in this weak-response limit. This is an explanatory derivation, distinct from the source’s two-state Ising normalization.
limitingCases: The expression cannot be extrapolated to T=0 or saturation.
pitfalls: It is not a ferromagnetic hysteresis law and does not include exchange correlations.
An Ising two-state moment has a different weak-field angular factor; do not import its normalized B coupling as SI tesla.

formulas.title: Curie–Weiss phenomenology
formulas.plain: A molecular-field correction shifts the Curie-law denominator.
conditions: Paramagnetic regime sufficiently far from transitions; fitted C and theta are model-dependent.
derivation: Assume an effective field H+lambda M and insert the Curie response.
Solve for M/H and absorb molecular-field coefficient into theta.

workedExample.inputs: C=0.1 K; T=300 K; theta=50 K

limitingCases: theta=0 recovers Curie behavior; the denominator divergence is not a literal finite-sample infinity.
pitfalls: Negative theta suggests dominant AFM correlations, not proof of a spin liquid or an ordering temperature.

formulas.title: Heisenberg exchange convention
formulas.plain: With this plus-sign convention, positive J favors antiparallel spin correlations.

variables.meaning: dimensionless spin operator at site i

conditions: Specify lattice, spin magnitude, boundary and omitted anisotropy/dipolar terms.
derivation: Reduce an electronic low-energy problem to spin degrees of freedom under declared assumptions.
For two spin1/2 particles, S1 dot S2 has eigenvalues−3/4 and+1/4.
limitingCases: For J<0 the triplet is lower in this convention.
pitfalls: Some authors write−J S dot S and reverse the meaning of positive J.

formulas.title: Classical triangular AFM counterexample
formulas.latex: E=J(\mathbf s_1\cdot\mathbf s_2+\mathbf s_2\cdot\mathbf s_3+\mathbf s_3\cdot\mathbf s_1)
formulas.plain: Three unit spins cannot make all three AFM bonds antiparallel.
conditions: Classical isotropic spins on a single triangular plaquette, zero field.
derivation: Write E=J(|s1+s2+s3|²−3)/2.
The lower bound occurs when the three vectors sum to zero.

workedExample.result: Emin=−1.5 J rather than the impossible−3 J

limitingCases: The 120degree classical ground state is ordered; frustration alone is not a quantum-spin-liquid proof.
pitfalls: Do not transfer a three-site classical minimum to an infinite quantum lattice without analysis.

formulas.title: Gilbert dynamics with positive gamma convention
formulas.latex: \dot{\mathbf m}=-\frac{\gamma}{1+\alpha^2}[\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff}+\alpha\mathbf m\times(\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff})]
formulas.plain: A unit magnetization precesses and damps with a declared positive gyromagnetic magnitude.

variables.meaning: effective induction including selected energy terms

conditions: Fixed saturation magnitude; differentiable effective energy; torque sources and temperature terms must be added explicitly.
derivation: Solve Gilbert implicit equation dm/dt=−gamma m cross B+alpha m cross dm/dt.
Use m dot dm/dt=0 to invert its tangent-plane operator.

workedExample.inputs: alpha=0; Bz=0.1 T; gamma=1.760e11 rad/(T s)
steps: Angular rate=gamma B=1.760e10 rad/s; divide by2pi.

limitingCases: With alpha=0 and static energy, precession conserves energy; alpha>0 removes energy for the consistent convention.
pitfalls: The selected MuMax paper prints a plus-prefactor gamma_LL form; this entry chooses positive gamma and an explicit minus sign. Check the source convention and actual precession direction before converting symbols.

formulas.title: Continuum exchange energy and effective field
formulas.plain: A smooth magnetization texture costs gradient energy and creates a restoring exchange field.
conditions: Constant A and Ms; slowly varying texture; appropriate fixed or natural boundaries.
derivation: Vary the gradient functional and integrate by parts.
Use Beff=−(1/Ms) deltaE/deltam as a volume functional derivative.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; sinusoidal wave k=1e7/m; Ms=8e5 A/m

limitingCases: Uniform m has zero exchange energy in this reference.
pitfalls: A mesh that cannot resolve rotation between cells misrepresents this continuum model.

formulas.title: Uniaxial anisotropy convention
formulas.plain: Positive K in this convention favors alignment along either easy-axis direction.
conditions: One uniaxial contribution with a chosen zero of energy; other anisotropies may coexist.
derivation: Expand a time-reversal-even scalar energy in the axis projection.
Subtract a constant so aligned states have zero energy.

workedExample.inputs: K=1e5 J/m³; m at45degrees to u

limitingCases: Parallel and antiparallel easy-axis states are degenerate under this term alone.
pitfalls: A negative coefficient changes the easy directions; do not infer them from the symbol K alone.

formulas.title: Interfacial DMI energy convention
formulas.plain: An inversion-asymmetric interfacial invariant favors one texture chirality.

variables.meaning: DMI energy per volume in effective thin-film convention

conditions: Thin-film interfacial symmetry; derivatives x,y only; boundary terms and normal orientation matter.
derivation: Construct a scalar linear in gradients allowed by interfacial symmetry.
A functional variation generates a chiral field plus nontrivial boundary conditions.

workedExample.inputs: One-dimensional cycloid m=(sin(qx),0,cos(qx)); q=1e7/m; D=1e-3 J/m²
steps: Substitution gives wD=Dq for this convention.
workedExample.result: wD=1e4 J/m³; reversing q reverses the sign

limitingCases: D=0 restores degeneracy of opposite chiralities for this term.
pitfalls: Bulk D m dot curl m is a different invariant; surface D_s in J/m must be divided by thickness to compare this effective D.

formulas.title: Magnetostatic exchange length
formulas.plain: Exchange and magnetostatic energy density scales define a useful resolution length.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Continuum ferromagnet; a characteristic scale, not a universal sufficient mesh certificate.
derivation: Balance gradient density A/ell² against mu0 Ms²/2.
Solve for ell.
limitingCases: Increasing A broadens the scale; increasing Ms reduces it.
pitfalls: DMI, anisotropy, interfaces and convergence may require smaller cells than this estimate.

formulas.title: Ideal one-dimensional domain wall
formulas.plain: Exchange and positive uniaxial anisotropy set a wall parameter and surface energy.

variables.meaning: wall profile parameter, not necessarily reported full width

conditions: One-dimensional180degree wall, no DMI or nonlocal demagnetizing correction; fixed opposite domains.
derivation: Minimize integral[A(theta prime)²+K sin²theta] dx.
First integral gives A(theta prime)²=K sin²theta; integrate the wall energy.
limitingCases: K→0 broadens the wall and invalidates isolated localized-wall assumptions in a finite sample.
pitfalls: Some papers call pi*Delta the wall width; define the convention before comparison.

formulas.title: Thin-film macrospin resonance
formulas.plain: Two restoring-field curvatures set the in-plane uniform-mode frequency.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
applied induction-equivalent mu0 H in plane
effective magnetization including declared perpendicular anisotropy

conditions: Uniform saturated film, small-angle motion, negligible damping shift; geometry/anisotropy convention specified.
derivation: Linearize torque around the in-plane equilibrium.
Combine two coupled transverse equations to obtain the product of restoring fields.

workedExample.inputs: gamma/(2pi)=28 GHz/T; BH=0.1 T; mu0 Meff=1 T

limitingCases: Setting Meff=0 reduces the expression to the simple Larmor frequency.
pitfalls: Do not insert H in A/m into a formula whose field arguments are tesla.

formulas.title: Exchange-dominated spin-wave limit
formulas.plain: A uniformly magnetized exchange continuum has quadratic wavevector dispersion in this limit.
conditions: Small-amplitude mode, uniform equilibrium, neglect dipolar dispersion/anisotropy or absorb appropriate constants in B0.
derivation: Insert a transverse plane wave into the exchange field.
Linearize undamped LLG to get precession with the shifted restoring field.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; Ms=8e5 A/m; k=1e7/m; gamma/(2pi)=28 GHz/T

limitingCases: As k→0 the exchange shift vanishes, but other gap terms may remain.
pitfalls: A measured film mode can be dipolar, exchange-dominated or mixed; this is not the entire magnon spectrum.

formulas.title: Skyrmion degree
formulas.plain: An oriented smooth two-dimensional spin texture maps the compactified plane to the unit sphere.
conditions: Fixed common boundary direction or compact domain; no singular point where |m| vanishes.
derivation: Integrate oriented area swept on the unit sphere and normalize by4pi.
For an axisymmetric texture reduce the integral to azimuthal winding and polar endpoint values.

workedExample.inputs: Azimuthal winding n=1; core theta=pi; boundary theta=0
workedExample.result: Q=−1; reversing orientation conventions can reverse its sign

limitingCases: A uniform state has Q=0; a boundary-unfixed partial texture need not give an integer.
pitfalls: Topological charge alone does not guarantee infinite lifetime or free energy; boundaries and singular events permit changes.

formulas.title: Spin Hall normalization
formulas.plain: A declared scalar spin Hall angle relates selected spin-angular-momentum flux to charge current density.

variables.meaning: signed conversion angle for stated axes

conditions: A specified material, transport geometry and spin polarization convention; tensor character suppressed only for one chosen component.
For this scalar example define charge along+x, flux along+z and polarization along+y; the signed thetaSH is defined for exactly that ordered axis choice.
derivation: Express spin flux as angular momentum per transported carrier.
Define thetaSH by the ratio of normalized transverse spin flux to charge flux.

workedExample.result: js=3.29106e-7 J/m² in the angular-momentum-flux convention

limitingCases: Changing spin-flux convention to charge-equivalent A/m² removes the hbar/(2e) prefactor.
pitfalls: A spin current is not an extra source of energy; injector electrical power and interface losses remain.
A spin Hall angle is a normalization-dependent conversion ratio, not an event probability; its magnitude is not universally bounded by1.

formulas.title: Damping-like spin–orbit torque
formulas.plain: A transverse angular-momentum input can reorient an ordered moment.
conditions: A selected torque term in an explicitly powered model; two-sublattice AFMs require the corresponding sublattice torques.
derivation: Resolve the injected spin into the tangent plane perpendicular to m.
Use m cross(s cross m)=s−(m dot s)m.

steps: The tangent direction is zhat; instantaneous rate scale is gamma BDL.
workedExample.result: dm/dt=1.76e8 zhat per second for this isolated term

limitingCases: Collinear s and m give zero torque for this term.
pitfalls: Switching depends on competing fields, pulse shape and heating; a torque expression is not a complete switching prediction.

formulas.title: London penetration in a half-space
formulas.plain: Local superfluid screening produces exponential equilibrium penetration in the simple half-space.
conditions: Static homogeneous London regime, planar surface, weak fields without vortices or strong nonlocality; bulk boundary B→0.
derivation: Combine curl js=−B/(mu0 lambdaL²) with stationary Ampere law and divergence B=0.
Select the decaying solution of the one-dimensional second-order equation.

workedExample.inputs: B(0)=1 mT; lambdaL=100 nm; z=200 nm

limitingCases: The growing exponential is excluded by the bulk boundary condition.
pitfalls: An ideal perfect conductor preserves initial flux; equilibrium Meissner expulsion needs more than infinite DC conductivity.

formulas.title: Superconducting flux quantum and fluxoid
formulas.plain: Single-valued pair phase quantizes a fluxoid, with magnetic flux alone recovered when the current term is negligible.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Closed contour in a coherent superconducting region; conventional2e pairing assumed; finite kinetic-current correction retained.
derivation: Integrate the gauge-invariant phase-gradient relation around a closed loop.
Phase change is2pi n; retain both vector-potential and supercurrent terms.

workedExample.inputs: h=6.62607015e-34 J s; e=1.602176634e-19 C; n=1; negligible current correction

limitingCases: In thin/high-kinetic-inductance loops, flux need not equal nPhi0 even though fluxoid does.
pitfalls: Flux quantization is not a universal quantization of arbitrary classical coil flux.

formulas.title: Ginzburg–Landau scale ratio
formulas.plain: Penetration and coherence scales organize superconducting interfaces and the orbital upper critical field.
conditions: Conventional isotropic GL description near its controlled transition regime; orbital limit, neglect paramagnetic/multiband modifications.
derivation: Nondimensionalize the GL equations by lambda and xi.
Linearized order-parameter onset in a uniform field gives the orbital length condition.

workedExample.inputs: lambda=100 nm; xi=10 nm; Phi0=2.067833848e-15 Wb
workedExample.result: kappa=10; Bc2≈3.29 T in this orbital approximation

limitingCases: The GL interface crossover is kappa=1/sqrt2 under the standard isotropic premises.
pitfalls: A material measured far from Tc may require a microscopic theory; this is not its universal critical field.

These sources support the Landau/phase and flux-quantum ingredients. A direct original GL/Hc2 source was not reviewed; the stated orbital formula is the explanatory linear-GL reconstruction, not a result inferred from the graphene preprint.

formulas.title: SI magnetoelectric cross derivative
formulas.plain: A reciprocal static cross response follows from one explicitly chosen thermodynamic potential.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
linear SI magnetoelectric tensor in this E,H convention

conditions: Equilibrium reversible small-field expansion at fixed declared thermodynamic variables; allowed tensor components depend on symmetry.
derivation: Use dg=−P dot dE−mu0 M dot dH for the selected material contribution.
Differentiate the bilinear cross term and equate mixed derivatives.
limitingCases: A coefficient defined using B or electric displacement instead of H/E has different factors and potentially units.
pitfalls: The layer-pseudospin polarizability in the selected bilayer paper is not silently identified with this bulk SI coefficient.

Only for volumetric M and a fixed uniform constitutive D=epsilon E can alpha_(E,H)=mu0*epsilon*(partial M/partial D). A two-dimensional layer moment may additionally require a thickness normalization; none is silently supplied.

formulas.title: NV axial Zeeman splitting
formulas.plain: A simple axial NV-center model converts a calibrated spin transition shift into a field projection.

variables.meaning: field projection along the known NV axis

conditions: Weak suitably aligned field, negligible transverse mixing/strain or independently calibrated corrections; approximate spin1 Hamiltonian.
derivation: Diagonalize D Sz²+gammae Bparallel Sz/(2pi) in frequency units.
Transition shifts are opposite for the m_s=±1 branches.

workedExample.result: Each branch shifts2.8 MHz; branch separation changes5.6 MHz

limitingCases: Temperature drift in D shifts both branches and can mimic single-line field changes.
pitfalls: One NV axis measures a projection, not an unconstrained three-component vector field.

formulas.title: Stray-field Fourier height filtering
formulas.plain: In a source-free half-space, lateral high-spatial-frequency magnetic structure decays with height.

variables.meaning: lateral Fourier field amplitude under a fixed transform convention

conditions: Planar Fourier analysis in a homogeneous source-free half-space; choose the solution decaying at infinity.
derivation: A scalar magnetic potential satisfies Laplace equation above sources.
Fourier transform laterally to obtain partial_z² potential=|k|² potential.
limitingCases: At k=0 the exponential is1, but boundary/source constraints can make particular uniform channels unobservable.
pitfalls: Exact back-propagation multiplies noise exponentially; regularization adds assumptions, not missing data.

formulas.title: Correlated first-order uncertainty propagation
formulas.plain: A local sensitivity Jacobian propagates a declared input covariance into output variance.

variables.meaning: input covariance, product of input units

conditions: Small enough uncertainties for linearization; covariance and model must be justified independently.
derivation: Taylor-expand output around nominal inputs.
Take variance of the linearized combination, retaining cross terms.

workedExample.inputs: y=x1−x2; each standard uncertainty=1 microtesla; correlationrho=0.9

limitingCases: Perfect common-mode correlation cancels in a difference only for matched sensitivities.
pitfalls: Ignoring covariance can overstate or understate uncertainty; no automatic95percent confidence follows from an arbitrary bound.

formulas.title: Two-dipole observation matrix and an explicit kernel
formulas.plain: A centred Bz measurement cannot distinguish two equally oriented dipoles at mirror-symmetric known positions.

variables.meaning: known dipole forward matrix for specified sensor/source geometry
common knownBz coupling coefficient at a symmetry-axis observation

conditions: Two ideal point dipoles atx=±a,y=z=0 withfixedz orientation;point-dipole far-field premise;known a andsensorheight h.
OneBz channel atx=y=0;the twounknowns are moments,notunknown positions/orientations.
derivation: The vacuum dipole kernel gives c=(mu0/4pi)(2h²−a²)/(a²+h²)^(5/2), wherea,h arelengths inmetres andmu0 isvacuum permeability.
Forc≠0 the1×2operator hasrank1andnullity1:K(1,−1)^T=0 although its onlyreturned singular value issqrt(2)|c|>0.

steps: AddBz atx=0.5m,z=2m:then the2×2matrixdeterminant is1.8688737689e−16[T/(A m²)]²andthe two-moment toy becomesinvertible.
workedExample.result: A singlemeasurement admits(2+t,1−t)for everyt;the off-axis secondmeasurementrecovers(2,1)withfloating errorbelow1e−12 inthis executedexample.

limitingCases: Repeatingcentredmeasurements atthreeheights2,3,4mstillhasrank1andnullity1becauseeachrow retains identicalcolumns.
Choosingh=a/sqrt2makesc=0andthe singleobservationrank0;anunmentionedzero-coupling casewouldinvalidatethe rank1claim.
pitfalls: Full-rank forthe restrictedtwo-moment toydoesnotprove uniquenessofanarbitrarycontinuum vector magnetization.
Invertibility isnot goodnoiseconditioning;report sensitivity,geometryuncertaintyandnoiseafterchoosing measurementunits/scales.

glossary.definition: B is magnetic induction in tesla; H is field intensity in ampere per metre. B=mu0(H+M) does not by itself assume a linear material.
International System of Units. The revised SI fixes h and e, while mu0 is experimentally inferred.
Ferromagnetic / antiferromagnetic / unequal opposing sublattice order; net moment alone does not specify a magnetic phase.
An antiferromagnetic sublattice-difference order parameter; its normalization must be declared.
Magnetoquasistatic approximation: retain induction while neglecting displacement current only under an appropriate scale analysis.
Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, an antisymmetric exchange contribution allowed by appropriate inversion-symmetry breaking.
Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert dynamics. Signed gyromagnetic conventions and B-versus-H choices must remain consistent.
Spin–orbit torque / spin-transfer torque. Both require an angular-momentum source and a complete electrical/thermal budget.
Density functional theory and increasingly structured exchange-correlation approximations; Hubbard U is an additional model parameter, not an automatic measured constant.
Nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond; an orientation-dependent spin sensor with its own Hamiltonian, calibration and bandwidth.
Quantum spin liquid: a proposed quantum phase requiring positive diagnostic evidence, not simply lack of observed order.
A long-period interference/registry pattern from lattice mismatch or twist; magnetic exchange depends on the actual relaxed structure.
Combined spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetry; neither a generic claim of magnetic absence nor a universal spin-degeneracy rule without the full symmetry setting.
A spin-wave excitation. A mode frequency, a driven resonance peak and a sensor spectral peak are different quantities.
Ginzburg–Landau coarse-grained order-parameter theory, especially controlled near a transition under its assumptions.
A system cannot deliver more energy than supplied plus initially stored energy over its stated ports and time window.
Verification checks implementation against a mathematical model; validation tests whether that model predicts the measured physical system.
Abstract-only, selected text and metadata identify different evidence levels; a source hash proves identity, not truth.
A statistical standard uncertainty, a deterministic numerical error bound and an assumed manufacturing tolerance are distinct.
Different contributions to angular-momentum transport can produce similar electrical/THz signals; a channel model is required.
Magnetic flux plus a supercurrent term; it is not always identical to magnetic flux through a loop.

openQuestions.question: How robust is phase coexistence to twist relaxation, defects and sensor transfer functions?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Correlated structural and vector-magnetic imaging with independently calibrated temperature and height.

openQuestions.question: Does the recent graphene observation uniquely identify a magnetic pairing mechanism?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Independent phase-sensitive and spin/valley-resolved constraints plus competing-phonon/electrostatic models.

formulas.title: Newtonian two-body attraction
formulas.plain: The separation vector points from source M to test mass m; the minus sign makes attraction.

variables.meaning: Source-to-test separation vector; scalar r in denominator is its positive Euclidean norm
Newtonian interaction potential energy introduced in derivation

conditions: Point masses or exterior spherical source
Nonrelativistic isolated interaction
derivation: Rotational symmetry fixes a radial force.
Potential U=-GMm/r gives F=-grad U.

steps: The force points toward the source.

limitingCases: M=0 gives zero force
pitfalls: At r=0 the point model is singular; an extended density must replace it.

formulas.title: Acceleration field
formulas.plain: Test-body acceleration is force divided by inertial mass under equality of inertial and passive gravitational mass.

variables.meaning: Separation vector; scalar r in denominator is its positive Euclidean norm

conditions: Test mass does not appreciably perturb source
Universal coupling assumed
derivation: Divide Newton force by m.
The test mass cancels algebraically.
limitingCases: Far from source magnitude tends to zero
pitfalls: Mass cancellation in the model is not an experimental proof of universal free fall.

formulas.title: Potential and conservative acceleration
formulas.plain: Potential is energy per unit test mass, fixed here to zero at infinity.
conditions: Static isolated spherical source
Zero potential at infinity
derivation: Integrate -GM/r² radially with boundary Phi(infinity)=0.
Differentiate to recover acceleration.

steps: Its gradient, not its arbitrary additive constant, affects acceleration.

limitingCases: Adding a constant leaves g unchanged
pitfalls: Do not identify a coordinate potential value with a directly measured absolute energy.

formulas.title: Poisson equation
formulas.plain: Mass density sources a Newtonian potential through a boundary-value problem.
conditions: Newtonian static or instantaneous approximation
Boundary conditions specified
Classical pointwise equation requires sufficient potential/source regularity; point masses and surface layers require a distributional interpretation at the singularsupport.
derivation: Use Gauss divergence theorem with flux integral of g=-4piG enclosed mass.
Set g=-grad Phi.
limitingCases: Vacuum has LaplacianPhi=0, not necessarily zero field
pitfalls: A harmonic potential can be nonzero; source equation without boundaries is not unique.
For Phi=-GM/r, the Laplacian vanishes only off r=0; distributionally it equals4piGM delta3 at the origin. No automaticglobalC2regularity follows from writing the equation.

formulas.title: Escape speed
formulas.plain: Zero energy at infinity determines the ideal minimum launch speed.
conditions: No atmosphere or other bodies
Newtonian point/exterior spherical source
derivation: Set specific energy v²/2-GM/r to zero.
Solve positive speed.
limitingCases: As r increases escape speed decreases
pitfalls: A local escape estimate neglects later thrust, drag and other gravitating bodies.

formulas.title: Circular orbital speed
formulas.plain: Centripetal acceleration equals gravitational acceleration for an ideal circular orbit.
conditions: Test-body circular orbit
Newtonian weak field
derivation: Set v²/r=GM/r².
Take positive magnitude.

steps: Compare escape speed at the same radius.

limitingCases: v_esc=sqrt2 v_c
pitfalls: Using altitude as radius instead of centre distance produces a large error.

formulas.title: Kepler period
formulas.plain: The relative two-body ellipse has a period determined by semimajor axis and total mass.
conditions: Isolated bound Newtonian two-body system
Ellipse with0<=e<1
derivation: Use angular-momentum conservation and ellipse area.
Insert the inverse-square orbit relation.
limitingCases: Circular limit preserves same period at radiusa
pitfalls: A planet perturbation or relativistic precession violates an exactly closed Kepler ellipse.

formulas.title: Vis-viva relation
formulas.plain: Instantaneous speed follows orbital energy; a is signed for hyperbolic convention.
conditions: Newtonian two-body potential
a>0 for ellipse and a<0 for hyperbola
derivation: Specific energy is-G(M+m)/(2a).
Equate to v²/2-G(M+m)/r.

steps: This is a scaled mathematical example.

limitingCases: a→infinity recovers parabolic escape
pitfalls: Not every numerical r,a pair is consistent with a physical orbit and angular momentum.

formulas.title: Specific mechanical energy
formulas.plain: Energy per unit test mass separates bound, parabolic and unbound Newtonian motion.
conditions: Static point potential
Negligible dissipation
derivation: Divide kinetic plus potential energy by test mass.
Use potential zero at infinity.
limitingCases: epsilon=0 marks parabolic energy
pitfalls: Negative energy does not specify a unique ellipse without angular momentum.

formulas.title: Specific angular momentum
formulas.plain: A central force conserves the orbital plane and areal velocity.
conditions: Central force
No external torque
derivation: Differentiate r×v.
Both v×v and r×radial acceleration vanish.
limitingCases: Pure radial motion has h=0
pitfalls: A nongravitational torque breaks conservation even if gravity remains central.

formulas.title: Point-mass tidal tensor
formulas.plain: Nearby free bodies separate radially and compress transversely in this Newtonian vacuum field.
conditions: Separation much smaller than r
Einstein sum over repeated j
derivation: Linearize g at displaced position.
Differentiate g=-GM r/r³; radial eigenvalue is2GM/r³.
limitingCases: Trace vanishes outside source
pitfalls: A uniform local acceleration can be transformed away; a tidal tensor generally cannot.

formulas.title: Spherical hydrostatic balance
formulas.plain: In a stationary Newtonian fluid, pressure decreases outward to oppose gravity.
conditions: Spherical static fluid
Newtonian pressure small relative to rest energy density
derivation: Balance pressure force on a thin shell with gravitational force.
Take shell thickness to zero.
limitingCases: Zero density yields zero pressure gradient
pitfalls: Compact stars require relativistic TOV and an equation of state, not this equation.

formulas.title: Schwarzschild length
formulas.plain: A mass defines the Schwarzschild horizon radius only for the stated nonrotating vacuum solution.
conditions: Nonrotating uncharged Schwarzschild spacetime
Do not infer a horizon from density alone
derivation: Solve1-2GM/(rc²)=0 in Schwarzschild metric.
This identifies a coordinate-horizon surface in the solution.

steps: Insert solar mass and SI constants.

limitingCases: r_s scales linearly with M
pitfalls: An ordinary star with radius much larger than r_s is not a black hole.

formulas.title: Spacetime interval
formulas.plain: A metric contracts coordinate displacements into an invariant interval.

variables.meaning: Metric components; units depend on chart

conditions: Signature(-,+,+,+)
x0=ct; all four Cartesian coordinates measured in metres
derivation: Apply the bilinear metric to a tangent displacement twice.
Under a coordinate change the component factors transform oppositely.
limitingCases: Null displacement has ds²=0
pitfalls: In spherical coordinates angular components have different coordinate units; metric entries are not all dimensionless there.

formulas.title: Timelike proper time
formulas.plain: An ideal comoving clock measures proper time along a timelike worldline.
conditions: Timelike path
Metric signature(-,+,+,+)
derivation: Normalize the tangent four-velocity.
Rearrange ds²=-c²dτ².
limitingCases: A null path has zero proper time but no rest-frame photon clock
pitfalls: Spacelike intervals do not define real elapsed proper time by this formula.

formulas.title: Levi-Civita connection
formulas.plain: Metric compatibility and zero torsion uniquely fix this connection.
conditions: Smooth nondegenerate metric
Torsion-free metric connection
derivation: Write covariant derivative of g equal to zero.
Permute three index equations and solve for Gamma.
limitingCases: Curvilinear flat coordinates can have nonzero Gamma
pitfalls: Gamma is not a tensor; nonzero coefficients alone do not establish curvature.

formulas.title: Affine geodesic equation
formulas.plain: A freely falling test body has zero covariant four-acceleration.

variables.meaning: Constant initial position in flat-worldline example

conditions: Timelike test body
No nongravitational force
Proper time is affine
derivation: Extremize proper-time action or parallel transport tangent.
Expand covariant derivative along the curve.
limitingCases: A coordinate acceleration need not vanish in curved coordinates
pitfalls: Accelerated rockets and extended spinning bodies need additional force or multipole equations.

formulas.title: Curvature sign convention
formulas.plain: Curvature measures failure of covariant derivatives to commute under the declared sign.
conditions: Smooth torsion-free connection
This sign convention fixes Ricci and Einstein signs
derivation: Apply[∇mu,∇nu] to a vector.
Collect derivative and quadratic connection terms.

steps: All derivatives and products are zero.
A coordinate change cannot change vanishing curvature.

limitingCases: Vanishing Gamma at one point does not force derivatives to vanish
pitfalls: Opposite Riemann conventions require coordinated sign changes; do not mix textbooks silently.

formulas.title: Ricci and scalar curvature
formulas.plain: Contractions summarize only part of the curvature tensor.
conditions: Same curvature sign as grav-f-riemann
Nondegenerate metric
derivation: Trace first and third Riemann slots.
Contract Ricci with inverse metric.

steps: Vacuum Einstein equation without Lambda gives Ricci zero.
workedExample.result: Ricci=0 and scalarR=0; full curvature need not vanish

limitingCases: Minkowski has full curvature zero
pitfalls: Ricci-flat does not mean gravity-free; black-hole tidal curvature is a counterexample.

formulas.title: Einstein field equation
formulas.plain: Local stress energy and spacetime curvature are related by a nonlinear metric equation.

variables.meaning: Stress-energy components in orthonormal SI frame

conditions: Signature(-,+,+,+) and declared curvature sign
Classical metric and specified matter
Gauge and initial/boundary data required
derivation: Vary Einstein-Hilbert plus matter action.
Discard/compensate boundary variations with a consistent boundary prescription.
limitingCases: Newtonian weak-field limit recovers Poisson with appropriate matter
pitfalls: Ten component equations include constraint/gauge structure; arbitrary metric components are not ten independent physical waves.

formulas.title: Perfect-fluid stress energy
formulas.plain: Energy density and isotropic pressure are defined in the fluid rest frame.
conditions: Local equilibrium and isotropic stress
u·u=-c²
No heat flux or viscosity
derivation: Rest-frame diagonal tensor is diag(epsilon,p,p,p).
Write the unique isotropic covariant combination of u and g.
limitingCases: Radiation has p=epsilon/3, not zero
pitfalls: Anisotropic collisionless matter or magnetic stresses are not perfect fluids.

formulas.title: Weak static potential in g00
formulas.plain: The Newtonian potential appears in the weak static metric under a suitable gauge.
conditions: |Phi|/c² much less than1
Static weak field and x0=ct
derivation: Expand the geodesic time-time connection.
Match slow-particle acceleration to-gradPhi.
limitingCases: Phi→0 gives flat time coefficient-1
pitfalls: This one component is not a complete metric for lensing or gravitational waves.

formulas.title: Newtonian limit of Einstein equation
formulas.plain: Slow matter and weak static curvature recover the Newtonian source law.
conditions: Slow pressureless matter
Weak nearly stationary field
Compatible metric/curvature conventions
derivation: Use weakmetric and trace-reversed Einstein equation.
Retain leading mass-density term.

steps: The harmonic exterior potential remains nonzero.

limitingCases: Strong fields require full Einstein dynamics
pitfalls: Dropping pressure is invalid for relativistic stars and early-universe radiation.

formulas.title: Static emitted/received photon-frequency ratio
formulas.plain: The locally measured photon frequency changes between static emitterA and receiverB. This is distinct from comparing identicallocal atomic-transition standards or their coordinate tickrates.
conditions: Static metric
Observers follow time-translation Killing flow
No additional Doppler shift
Matter/clockcoupling is metric and the same localtransitionstandard is used; nonmetric coupling or varyingconstants need separate modeling.
g00(A)<0 andg00(B)<0: both observers follow a timelike staticKillingflow, not a horizon or ergoregion where that staticclock construction fails.
derivation: Conserve photon Killing energy.
Convert coordinate energy to local proper-time frequency.
limitingCases: Identical potentials give unit ratio
pitfalls: Swapping emitter and receiver reverses the ratio; moving clocks require velocity terms.

Higher static clocks accumulate moreproper time per unit staticcoordinate time, while a photon climbing outward is received redshifted. These reciprocalcomparisons must not be described with one unsignedclockshift.

formulas.title: Schwarzschild line element
formulas.plain: Static spherical vacuum has a horizon-coordinate singularity at r_s.
conditions: Nonrotating uncharged vacuum exterior
r>r_s for static observers
derivation: Solve spherical vacuum field equations with asymptotic flatness.
Use areal radius so spheres have area4pi r².
limitingCases: r≫r_s approaches flat spherical metric
pitfalls: r=r_s is not a material surface; regular coordinates cross it. Kerr requires spin terms.

formulas.title: Schwarzschild innermost stable circular orbit
formulas.plain: Marginal radial stability fixes the ISCO for test-particle timelike circular geodesics.
conditions: Nonspinning black hole
Negligible particle self-force
Timelike geodesic
derivation: Set first derivative of radial effective potential to zero.
Set its second derivative to zero for marginal stability.
limitingCases: Kerr spin changes ISCO strongly
pitfalls: The photon orbit at3GM/c² is different from the timelike ISCO.

formulas.title: Leading periapsis advance
formulas.plain: Weak-field relativistic correction rotates an ideal elliptical orbit per revolution.
conditions: Weak field
Slow bound test orbit
0<=e<1; perturbative expansion
derivation: Perturb the Schwarzschild orbit equation by3GMu²/c².
Extract secular phase shift of radial oscillation.

steps: Circular limit refers to nearby slightly eccentric epicycles.

limitingCases: G M/(a c²)→0 gives Newton closure
pitfalls: As e→1 at fixeda, pericentre may leave the weak-field regime.

formulas.title: Weak Schwarzschild light deflection
formulas.plain: Both time and spatial metric curvature contribute to the leading asymptotic bending.
conditions: Weak deflection b≫r_s
Source and observer far from isolated lens
derivation: Integrate the perturbed null geodesic.
Retain first order inGM/(bc²).
limitingCases: b→infinity gives zero deflection
pitfalls: Near the photon region multiple looping images require strong-field ray tracing.

formulas.title: Leading Shapiro delay
formulas.plain: A nearly conjunction ray accumulates an additional propagation delay relative to flat geometry.
conditions: Weak static spherical field
rA,rB≫b
One-way convention
derivation: Integrate leading null coordinate travel time along nearly straight ray.
Separate the geometry-dependent flat travel time.
limitingCases: Delay vanishes with M
pitfalls: A radar round trip normally doubles a symmetric one-way result; coordinates and reference path must be specified.

formulas.title: First Friedmann equation
formulas.plain: Expansion, density, spatial curvature and Lambda obey a homogeneous-background constraint.
conditions: FLRW homogeneity/isotropy
k has unitsm^-2 in this normalizeda convention
ClassicalGR
derivation: Insert FLRW metric into00 Einstein component.
Use comoving perfect-fluid stress energy.

workedExample.units: s^-2 for equation; J/m³ for example

limitingCases: Vacuum with positiveLambda gives constantH
pitfalls: Using k=±1 while keeping a dimensionless requires a separate curvature scale; conventions must not be mixed.

formulas.title: FLRW acceleration equation
formulas.plain: Pressure contributes to gravitational deceleration as well as energy density.
conditions: FLRW perfect-fluid background
Cosmic proper time for comoving observers
derivation: Combine spatial and temporal Einstein components.
Use isotropy to replace stresses byp.

steps: The fluid contribution has positive acceleration.

limitingCases: Pressureless positive density decelerates withoutLambda
pitfalls: Acceleration alone does not identify a unique particle or modified-gravity mechanism.

formulas.title: Cosmological continuity
formulas.plain: An isolated homogeneous fluid loses or gains energy density through expansion work.
conditions: Separately conserved fluid
No inter-sector energy transfer
derivation: Use covariant stress-energy conservation.
Equivalently apply d(epsilon a³)=-p d(a³).
limitingCases: p=-epsilon yields constant density
pitfalls: Interacting dark sectors require a source term and cannot use separate conservation unchanged.

formulas.title: Constant equation-of-state scaling
formulas.plain: A constantw closes the homogeneous continuity equation.
conditions: Constantw
Separately conserved component
derivation: Divide continuity byH epsilon.
Integrate dln epsilon=-3(1+w)dln a.
limitingCases: Dustw0 givesa^-3; vacuumw-1 givesconstant
pitfalls: A fitted time-varyingw cannot be replaced by one constant across all epochs.

formulas.title: Critical energy density
formulas.plain: Critical energy density corresponds to flatness when all contributions are accounted consistently.
conditions: FLRW background
Do not double-countLambda as both fluid and explicit term
derivation: Set curvature contribution to zero in Friedmann.
Solve for total effective energy density.
limitingCases: H→0 gives zero critical density
pitfalls: Energy density epsilon_c differs byc² from mass density rho_c.

formulas.title: Flat FLRW luminosity distance
formulas.plain: Flux dilution includes both geometric distance and photon redshift/time dilation.
conditions: Spatially flat FLRW
Transparent metric photon propagation
Standard luminosity-distance definition
derivation: Integrate radial null trajectory for comoving distance.
Multiply by1+z for received flux.
limitingCases: z≪1 gives Hubble law
pitfalls: Curvature requires a transverse-distance function; luminosity and angular-diameter distance are not interchangeable.

formulas.title: CPL equation of state
formulas.plain: Two parameters summarize a chosen time-varying dark-energy history.

variables.meaning: Dark-energy density and its presentvalue introduced in the continuityderivation

conditions: Phenomenological parameterization
Specified redshift range and priors
derivation: The parameterization defines w(a)=w0+wa(1-a); it is not a uniquelyderivedmicroscopic field.
Insert into separatelyconserved fluid equation dln(epsilon)/dln(a)=-3[1+w(a)].
Integration froma=1 gives epsilon/epsilon0=a^[-3(1+w0+wa)] exp[-3wa(1-a)], matching the densityratio inDESIDR2Eq10 after consistent mass/energy conversion.
limitingCases: w0=-1,wa=0 recoversLambda equation of state
pitfalls: A preference for this model is not direct detection of a new dark-energy particle.
The analyticdensityratio does not validate the chosenw(a), establish stability, or identify the physicalcause of a distance-fit preference.

formulas.title: Far-zone quadrupole strain
formulas.plain: Slow-source far-zone radiation is determined by a transverse trace-free mass-quadrupole projection.
conditions: Weak far-zone radiation
Slow source
Distance much greater than source size/wavelength scale as appropriate
derivation: Solve linearized retarded metric equation.
Use mass/momentum conservation to express leading radiation in quadrupole terms.

steps: Projection and orientation are assumed in suppliedQTT.

limitingCases: Static quadrupole has zero second derivative and no radiation
pitfalls: Near-zone fields and relativistic merger require stronger methods.

formulas.title: Binary chirp mass
formulas.plain: A mass combination controls leading inspiral phase evolution.
conditions: Positive masses
Leading quasi-circular inspiral
derivation: Combine reduced mass and total mass in quadrupole energy balance.
Rewrite aseta^(3/5) totalmass.
limitingCases: Extreme mass ratio hasMchirp much below total mass
pitfalls: Detector-frame mass is redshifted by1+z; waveform masses alone do not fix source redshift.

formulas.title: Leading chirp-rate law
formulas.plain: Gravitational-wave frequency rises as a quasi-circular binary loses orbital energy.
conditions: Leading quadrupole order
Quasi-circular adiabatic inspiral
Not merger
derivation: Differentiate Newtonian orbital energy with frequency.
Equate its loss to quadrupole radiated power.
limitingCases: Smallf strongly suppresses chirp
pitfalls: Spins, eccentricity and post-Newtonian effects alter the waveform; do not extrapolate through merger.

formulas.title: Leading circular-binary amplitude scale
formulas.plain: An amplitude scale depends on distance and mass as well as frequency.

variables.meaning: Chirp mass consistent with frequency frame

conditions: Leading circular inspiral
Polarization/inclination factors applied separately
Cosmological redshift convention consistent
derivation: Insert circular orbit quadrupole into far-zone formula.
Use Kepler relation to remove orbital separation.
limitingCases: Doubling distance halves amplitude
pitfalls: Inclination-distance degeneracy prevents unique distance from one scalar amplitude.

formulas.title: Damped ringdown component
formulas.plain: A selected quasinormal contribution has a decay time and oscillation frequency.

variables.meaning: Complex angular frequency in exp(-i omega t) convention

conditions: Linear black-hole perturbation after a justified start
One selected mode
No growing instability assumed
derivation: Use complexfrequencyomega=2pi fR-i/tau withexp(-iomega t).
Take a real component with adjusted phase.
limitingCases: tau→infinity removes damping
pitfalls: A short fitted damped sinusoid alone does not establish a Kerr spectrum or unique mode identification.

formulas.title: Hellings–Downs angular curve
formulas.plain: The ideal isotropic tensor-background correlation has a distinctive angular shape.
conditions: GR transverse tensor polarizations
Isotropic unpolarized stochastic background
Standard pulsar-term averaging and normalization
derivation: Average products of pulsar antenna responses over sky directions.
Retain autocorrelation normalization separately.
limitingCases: For distinct co-aligned pulsars xlnx→0 andzeta→1/2
pitfalls: Spatially common red noise without the correlation pattern is not equivalent evidence for this model.

formulas.title: Semiclassical Einstein equation
formulas.plain: A classical metric is sourced by a renormalized quantum stress expectation in a chosen state.
conditions: Specified quantum state and renormalization prescription
Controlled stress fluctuations
Not asserted fundamental at all scales
derivation: Vary a suitable renormalized effective action or use mean-field approximation.
Include necessary gravitational counterterms when required.

steps: Set the reference vacuum stress to zero consistently.
Flat metric is then a conditional solution.

limitingCases: Large stress fluctuations can invalidate a mean-source approximation
pitfalls: It is not a complete theory of quantum metric fluctuations.

formulas.title: Planck length
formulas.plain: A dimensional length combines quantum action, gravity and relativity.
conditions: SI constants
Dimensional scale, not a derived universal minimum distance
derivation: Require a length monomial inħ,G,c.
Solve dimensions for exponents1/2,1/2,-3/2.
limitingCases: G→0 makes this gravity-dependent scale vanish
pitfalls: Dimensional analysis does not establish measured area discreteness or a UV completion.

formulas.title: Schwarzschild Hawking temperature
formulas.plain: A nonrotating black hole has a semiclassical temperature defined relative to asymptotic time.

variables.meaning: Surface gravity with asymptotic time normalization

conditions: Quantum fields on a semiclassical Schwarzschild background
Large enough mass for small curvature at horizon
Asymptotic normalization
derivation: Relate horizon surfacegravity to thermal periodicity or Bogoliubov particle creation.
Useκ=c⁴/(4GM) andkBT=ħκ/(2pi c).

steps: The predicted temperature is extremely low.

limitingCases: LargerM gives lowerTH
pitfalls: This is not a direct detection of Hawking radiation from an astrophysical black hole.

glossary.definition: General relativity, a classical metric theory with stated matter coupling.
Parameterized post-Newtonian framework for weak-field metric comparisons.
Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker homogeneous/isotropic background.
Baryon acoustic oscillations, a statistical clustering-distance ruler.
Cosmic microwave background; likelihood constraints depend on a cosmological model.
Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument survey. DR1 andDR2refer to distinct observation/release analyses.
Pulsar timing array, a network of astronomical clocks probing low-frequency correlations.
Event Horizon Telescope very-long-baseline interferometric imaging collaboration.
Gravitational Wave Open Science Center; data are not automatically cleaned measurements of everymodelparameter.
Transverse-traceless projection defined relative to a propagation direction/background.
Quasinormalmode with specified outgoing/ingoingboundaryconditions andcomplexfrequency.
Innermost stable circular orbit under a specified spacetime andtest-particlemodel.
Effective field theory, a scale-separated expansion with matchedcoefficients andcontrolleddomain.
Anti-de Sitter/conformal-field-theory correspondence in specified regimes, not a generic measureduniverseidentity.
Loop quantum gravity; kinematics,physicalconstraints andsemiclassicallimits require separateevidence.
Weak equivalenceprinciple concerning universaltest-bodyfreefall.
State of the art; this atlas provides a dated selectedcorpus, not an exhaustive latestsurvey.
A model-dependent tail or Gaussian-equivalent shorthand; not probability a theory istrue.
Timecoordinate expressed as a length; cosmicproper time is still measured inseconds.
rho haskg/m³ while epsilon hasJ/m³. They differ byc² only in the appropriate rest-energy relation.
R^rho_sigmamunu=partial_muGamma^rho_nusigma-partial_nuGamma^rho_musigma+Gamma^rho_mulambdaGamma^lambda_nusigma-Gamma^rho_nulambdaGamma^lambda_musigma; Ricci=R^rho_sigmarhonu.
