nodes.title: Coulomb force with an oriented separation
nodes.plain: The force on charge1 points from2 to1 for like signs.
conditions: Stationary point charges in vacuum, distinct positions; microscopic linear superposition.
derivation: Spherical symmetry fixes a radial field.
Gauss flux fixes its coefficient; multiply the field of2 by q1.
limitingCases: Force vanishes when either charge is zero; doubles if one charge doubles.
pitfalls: The r→0 singularity is not a finite-size charge or contact-force model.

nodes.title: Electric field as a linear source map
nodes.latex: \mathbf E(\mathbf r)=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\int\rho(\mathbf r\prime)\frac{\mathbf r-\mathbf r\prime}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r\prime|^3}\,d^3r\prime
nodes.plain: Integrate vector contributions, not field magnitudes.
conditions: Localized integrable source in unbounded vacuum; singular sources need distributions or a prescribed principal value.
derivation: Replace a charge by rho*dV.
Add oriented Coulomb contributions and pass to the continuum integral.

workedExample.inputs: Two equal charges at±a; observe the midpoint
steps: Pair each vector with its opposite.
workedExample.result: E=0 by symmetry despite a nonzero potential.

limitingCases: Far from a localized distribution, its net charge gives the leading field.
pitfalls: Zero field at one point does not imply no charge or zero field energy.

nodes.title: Gauss law and what flux measures
nodes.plain: Flux depends on enclosed total charge; solving for local field additionally needs symmetry.
conditions: Closed oriented surface; microscopic vacuum form includes bound as well as free charge.
derivation: Integrate the inverse-square field over solid angle.
Use superposition or the divergence theorem to obtain divE=rho/epsilon0.
limitingCases: A charge outside contributes zero net flux, but generally nonzero local field.
pitfalls: Replacing E by a uniform magnitude on an arbitrary Gaussian surface is unjustified.

nodes.title: Potential, gauge and path independence
nodes.plain: A potential difference is work per unit positive test charge with the stated minus sign.
conditions: Electrostatic curlE=0 on a simply connected domain, or a globally defined conservative field.
derivation: Apply Stokes theorem to zero curl.
Define phi relative to one reference; adding a constant leaves E unchanged.

workedExample.inputs: Uniform E=100V/m along+x; B lies0.02m aboveA in x

limitingCases: A closed-loop integral is zero in electrostatics.
pitfalls: Time-varying magnetic flux can make the electric field nonconservative; a scalar potential alone then fails.

nodes.title: Heterogeneous-permittivity Poisson equation
nodes.plain: Free charge, constitutive response and boundary data determine the potential together.
conditions: Local linear dielectric; tensor bounded and coercive; suitable Dirichlet/Neumann data.
derivation: Combine D=epsilonE, E=−gradphi and divD=rho_f.
Do not move spatially varying epsilon outside the divergence.

workedExample.inputs: 1D slab with constant epsilon and uniform rho; phi(0)=phi(L)=0

limitingCases: For constant scalar epsilon this becomes −epsilon*Laplacian(phi)=rho_f.
pitfalls: Using epsilon*Laplacian(phi) across a jump erases the interface condition.

nodes.title: Laplace uniqueness and the missing constant
nodes.plain: Two solutions with identical admissible data differ only by a gauge constant; Dirichlet data fixes it.

variables.meaning: electrostatic potential in displayed Laplace equation

conditions: Connected bounded Lipschitz domain; real scalar epsilon uniformly positive. The displayed Laplace equation assumes spatially constant epsilon; heterogeneous epsilon uses the divergence-form operator of es-f05.

Compare potentials with the same sources and admissible boundary traces. A Dirichlet set of positive measure fixes the gauge; all-Neumann data require compatibility and a specified additive constant/mean. Disconnected regions need these conditions componentwise.
derivation: Subtract the PDEs.
Multiply by the difference and integrate by parts; boundary terms vanish.
Positive epsilon forces equal gradients.

steps: Both phi=0 and phi=7V solve the same gradient problem.
workedExample.result: Only the additive constant is undetermined.

limitingCases: With two fixed endpoint voltages in1D, phi is their linear interpolation.
pitfalls: All-Neumann solvability also needs total-charge/flux compatibility, not just a numerical gauge.

nodes.title: Electrostatic interface conditions
nodes.latex: \mathbf n\cdot(\mathbf D_2-\mathbf D_1)=\sigma_f,\qquad\mathbf n\times(\mathbf E_2-\mathbf E_1)=0
nodes.plain: The normal points from medium1 to2; a free surface sheet jumps normal D, not generically normal E.
conditions: Ideal zero-thickness interface without a prescribed dipole-sheet potential jump; static fields.
derivation: Shrink a Gaussian pillbox to the interface.
Shrink a rectangular Faraday loop to obtain tangential continuity.

workedExample.inputs: No free sheet; epsilon2=2epsilon1; field normal

limitingCases: Equal permittivities and zero sheet give continuous E.
pitfalls: A conducting surface may carry induced free charge; setting sigma_f=0 there is usually wrong.

nodes.title: Localized-source far-field expansion
nodes.latex: \phi(\mathbf r)=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\frac Qr+\frac{\mathbf p\cdot\widehat{\mathbf r}}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right),\quad\mathbf p=\int\mathbf r\prime\rho\,dV\prime
nodes.plain: Net charge and dipole moment organize the leading spatial decay.
conditions: Source support lies within radius a and r>a; origin matters when Q is nonzero.
derivation: Expand1/|r−rprime| in rprime/r.
Integrate successive angular moments.

workedExample.inputs: Charges±q separated by d; r≫d on the axis

limitingCases: For Q=0 the dipole may lead; if p also vanishes, higher moments control.
pitfalls: A visually symmetric image is not a measured charge distribution or a justified multipole truncation.

nodes.title: Dipole energy and a nonuniform field force
nodes.latex: U=-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf E,\quad\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf p\times\mathbf E,\quad\mathbf F=\nabla(\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf E)
nodes.plain: Orientation energy and translation force are different consequences of an imposed field.
conditions: Small fixed dipole, field varies slowly across it; no induced-dipole factor or self-field included.
derivation: Sum forces and work on the two opposite charges.
Retain the first order in separation.

steps: The cross product vanishes and the gradient is zero.

limitingCases: A uniform field can rotate a misaligned dipole without translating it.
pitfalls: For a linearly induced dipole p=alphaE, its charging energy has a factor1/2.

nodes.title: Capacitance and the parallel-plate approximation
nodes.plain: Capacitance is a geometry/material/boundary response, not charge stored without a voltage reference.
conditions: Linear dielectric; d much smaller than lateral electrode size; opposing charges and negligible fringing.
derivation: Gauss law gives E≈Q/(epsilonA).
Integrate DeltaV≈Ed and divide Q by voltage.
limitingCases: C doubles with area and halves with gap in this limit.
pitfalls: Small or edge-dominated electrodes require a field solution; measured parasitics add capacitance.

nodes.title: Maxwell capacitance matrix
nodes.latex: Q_i=\sum_j C_{ij}V_j,\qquad U=\tfrac12\mathbf V^T\mathbf C\mathbf V
nodes.plain: A multi-electrode system needs an explicitly grounded reference or a retained gauge mode.
conditions: Linear reciprocal electrostatics with fixed conductor geometry; the full isolated matrix is gauge singular.
derivation: Linearity lets each electrode basis voltage define a response column.
Reciprocity gives symmetry; integrate charging work.

workedExample.inputs: Two isolated conductors with mutual capacitance C
workedExample.result: Adding the same voltage to both leaves charges unchanged.

limitingCases: After grounding one electrode the remaining matrix is positive on allowed voltages.
pitfalls: Circuit mutual capacitances and off-diagonal Maxwell coefficients differ in sign convention.

nodes.title: Stored field energy and nonlinear qualification
nodes.latex: U=\tfrac12\int\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf D\,dV;\qquad w(\mathbf D)=\int_0^{\mathbf D}\mathbf E(\mathbf D\prime)\cdot d\mathbf D\prime
nodes.plain: The one-half expression requires a linear reversible constitutive relation; nonlinear work needs the constitutive path.
conditions: Lossless reversible local medium; fixed mechanical state. First equality applies only to linear D(E).
derivation: Charge the system quasistatically: incremental work is E·dD.
Integrate along the reversible constitutive curve.
limitingCases: At zero field a reference with zero remanent energy can be assigned U=0.
pitfalls: Ferroelectric hysteresis, losses and electrostriction cannot be hidden inside a constant epsilon.

nodes.title: Force at fixed voltage versus fixed charge
nodes.plain: The voltage source changes the appropriate thermodynamic potential; differentiating field energy at fixed V alone gives the wrong sign.

variables.meaning: voltage-controlled electric thermodynamic potential including source work
stored field energy Q²/(2C)=CV²/2 at the specified state
constant dielectric permittivity in the plate example
overlap area in the plate example

conditions: Quasistatic linear capacitor; mechanical coordinate and controlled electrical ensemble explicitly fixed.
derivation: At fixed Q, force is minus the x derivative of U=Q²/(2C).
At fixed V, source work is deltaW_source=V*deltaQ. Legendre transform G=U−VQ=−CV²/2; F=−partialG/partialx at fixed V.
Differentiate the controlled potential, not field energy with the source omitted.

workedExample.inputs: x is plate separation and C=epsilonA/x

limitingCases: At V=0 with no trapped charge, this ideal force vanishes.
pitfalls: A power supply is an energy port; electrostatic attraction does not create energy.
Changing the plate gap at fixed V returns or draws charge through the supply; electrical source work and external mechanical work must both appear in the energy balance.

nodes.title: Maxwell stress in a simple dielectric
nodes.plain: Stress converts a solved field to a force under a declared material-mechanics model.
conditions: Static, homogeneous isotropic medium or vacuum integration surface; mechanical/electrostrictive terms must be handled consistently in matter.
derivation: Balance momentum across a surface.
The normal field produces pressure epsilonE²/2 on an ideal conductor.

workedExample.inputs: Vacuum E=1e5V/m normal to a conductor

limitingCases: For zero field this field-only stress vanishes.
pitfalls: Applying the vacuum expression inside a deformable nonlinear dielectric can omit material stresses.

nodes.title: Polarization and electric displacement
nodes.plain: D packages free-charge bookkeeping; P records dipole moment per volume.
conditions: Second relation assumes local linear isotropic response without remanence; first is the standard macroscopic definition.
derivation: Coarse-grain microscopic dipoles.
Separate imposed/free charge from bound polarization charge.
limitingCases: Vacuum has P=0 and D=epsilon0E.
pitfalls: D is not universally the physical microscopic field and need not be continuous normally.

nodes.title: Bound volume and surface charge
nodes.plain: A polarized body may have no volume charge and still carry opposite bound surface sheets.
conditions: Macroscopic polarization with resolved boundary; discontinuities can be represented distributionally.
derivation: Integrate dipole charge over a small volume.
Apply the divergence theorem to transfer termination of P to the surface.

steps: divP=0 in the interior; top/bottom normals reverse.
workedExample.result: Surface sheets+P0 and−P0; no bulk rho_b.

limitingCases: A uniform polarization in an infinite periodic model has no physical outer surface.
pitfalls: Do not add sigma_b twice when using an epsilon-based interface formulation.

nodes.title: Anisotropic electrostatic energy
nodes.plain: Anisotropy changes direction as well as magnitude; a stable reciprocal dielectric has positive quadratic energy.
conditions: Real symmetric positive-definite tensor in a local quasistatic reciprocal model.
derivation: Differentiate the quadratic energy with respect to E.
Diagonalize the tensor along principal axes.

workedExample.result: D is not parallel to E; w=3epsilon0E0².

limitingCases: Scalar epsilon is the isotropic special case.
pitfalls: A frequency-dependent negative real permittivity requires dispersive energy; this static positive-energy model is not applicable.

nodes.title: Clausius–Mossotti local-field model
nodes.plain: A molecular polarizability becomes a bulk response only after a local-field hypothesis.
conditions: Isotropic weakly interacting polarizable units with Lorentz spherical-cavity local field; no strong correlations or permanent-dipole complications.
derivation: Use E_local=E+P/(3epsilon0).
Substitute P=n*alpha_m*E_local and solve for susceptibility.
limitingCases: At dilute n, chi_e≈nalpha_m/epsilon0.
pitfalls: The apparent denominator singularity signals model breakdown, not a universal ferroelectric transition prediction.

nodes.title: Planar dielectric image charge
nodes.plain: An image is an auxiliary mathematical charge reproducing boundary data on one side.
conditions: Infinite planar interface, linear isotropic homogeneous half-spaces, no prescribed free sheet; qprime is used for the medium1 potential.
derivation: Write real+image Green functions.
Match tangential E and normal D at the plane.
limitingCases: Equal media give no image; conductor limit epsilon2→infinity gives−q.
pitfalls: The image is not a second physical source; evaluating self-force must exclude the real charge singularity.

nodes.title: Landau differential stability
nodes.plain: A homogeneous stationary branch is not necessarily a stable state.
conditions: Phenomenological homogeneous mean-field expansion; stability requires second derivative positive with the controlled ensemble and any circuit/domain terms included.

The stationary/curvature conditions are local. Global equilibrium requires comparing admissible minima and nonuniform/domain states; if treating the polynomial globally, its highest retained even-power coefficient must make it bounded below.
derivation: Set derivative of f with respect to P to zero.
Differentiate E(P): slope=a+3bP²+5cP⁴.

workedExample.result: P=E/a is a stable linear branch.

limitingCases: If a<0,b>0 at E=0, P=0 is unstable and nonzero minima appear.
pitfalls: Domain walls, gradients, strain and switching kinetics are omitted; fitted coefficients are not universal constants.

nodes.title: Series stabilization and negative differential capacitance
nodes.plain: A negative subsystem slope can coexist with a positive total curvature under constrained coupling.
conditions: Same incremental charge in a series quasistatic model; total free-energy curvature positive; leakage and domain alternatives must be checked.
derivation: Sum incremental voltages dV=dQ/Cs+dQ/Cf.
Positive dV/dQ is the local total-system stability requirement.

workedExample.result: Ctot=2nF; if Cf=−.5nF the total curvature is negative.

limitingCases: Cf→infinity leaves Ctot=Cs.
pitfalls: A transient negative dQ/dV trace alone does not demonstrate stable equilibrium negative capacitance or energy creation.

nodes.title: Boltzmann ion distribution
nodes.plain: Equilibrium ion density follows a balance of ideal mixing entropy and electrostatic energy.
conditions: Dilute ideal ions at thermal equilibrium, uniform temperature, reservoir chemical potentials and point-ion mean field.
derivation: Set mu_i=kBT*ln(n_i)+z_i*e*psi+constant equal to its reservoir value.
Exponentiate.
limitingCases: At psi=0 the reservoir concentration is recovered.
pitfalls: Divergent accumulation at a highly charged wall is a point-ion model failure.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Poisson–Boltzmann equation
nodes.plain: The electrostatic field and ion distribution must be solved self-consistently.
conditions: Mean-field point ions, local continuum dielectric, equilibrium reservoir and specified wall conditions; reservoir electroneutrality is required.
derivation: Insert ideal Boltzmann densities into Poisson.
For symmetric1:1 salt the mobile charge is−2en_b*sinh(epsi/kBT).

workedExample.inputs: Neutral homogeneous reservoir with no fixed charge
steps: Choose psi=0 and equal cation/anion densities.
workedExample.result: Both sides vanish; psi=0 is a solution.

limitingCases: Linearization gives Debye–Hückel only for small dimensionless potential.
pitfalls: Mean-field PB neglects ion correlations, finite size, hydration and image self-energy unless extended.

nodes.title: Debye screening length
nodes.plain: Screening length depends on ionic strength, dielectric response and temperature, not charge signs alone.
conditions: Linearized dilute PB in a uniform bulk electrolyte; concentrations converted to number density.
derivation: Expand exp(−zi*u) to first order.
The zeroth-order charge cancels by electroneutrality; remaining coefficient is kappa².
limitingCases: Increasing concentration100-fold reduces lambdaD tenfold in this model.
pitfalls: Molarity is mol/L; inserting1mM as0.001mol/m³ gives a spurious factor sqrt1000.

nodes.title: Screened point-charge Green function
nodes.plain: A Yukawa form is a linear-response Green function, not the exact nonlinear field near a highly charged ion.
conditions: Unbounded homogeneous linearized electrolyte; small perturbation away from the source core.
derivation: Solve (−Laplacian+kappa²)psi=qdelta/epsilon.
Spherical decay and the Coulomb singular flux fix the coefficient.

workedExample.result: Potential is0.368 of the corresponding unscreened value.

limitingCases: kappa→0 restores the Coulomb potential.
pitfalls: A fitted decay length in concentrated solutions need not equal the dilute Debye length.

nodes.title: Planar Grahame relation
nodes.plain: For a planar symmetric monovalent diffuse layer, surface charge and potential are nonlinearly related.

variables.meaning: bulk density of each salt species

conditions: Single infinite planar surface,1:1 PB electrolyte, no Stern layer or correlations, vanishing bulk potential/field. Positive psi0 corresponds to positive sigma.
derivation: Multiply the1D PB equation by psi prime.
Integrate once using the bulk boundary condition, then use normal Gauss law.
limitingCases: At psi0=0 the charge is zero.
pitfalls: Curvature, finite ion size and compact-layer voltage invalidate direct use as an electrode-total capacitance.

nodes.title: A lattice-gas crowding correction
nodes.plain: A finite site volume prevents point-ion density divergence within one explicit modified mean-field model.
conditions: Equal-size symmetric ions with lattice-gas entropy, bulk volume fraction2vn_b<1; mean field still neglects electrostatic correlations.
derivation: Include the solvent-vacancy entropy in chemical potentials.
Solve their equilibrium ratios under site exclusion.
limitingCases: v→0 recovers ideal Boltzmann densities.
pitfalls: A hard density cap is not a quantitative theory of hydration, asymmetric ions or oscillatory packing layers.

nodes.title: Bjerrum length and planar coupling parameter
nodes.plain: Thermal energy versus Coulomb energy and interfacial charge density determine whether independent-ion intuition is credible.

variables.meaning: Gouy–Chapman wall length under this valence/surface-charge convention

conditions: Xi convention is for a planar counterion-only charged wall; added salt, dielectric images and finite ion sizes require separate parameters.
derivation: Define ellB by setting the unit-charge Coulomb energy at that length equal to kBT.
For a planar wall define muGC=e/(2πz ellB |sigma|); combining z²ellB/muGC gives the displayed Xi.
This is a declared standard-model nondimensionalization, independently reconstructed here, not a theorem attributed to the modern interface/slab papers.

workedExample.result: Xi≈3.2; z=3 gives≈86 under the same convention.

limitingCases: Increasing valence changes Xi cubically in this wall model.
pitfalls: A single Xi threshold does not universally certify mean-field validity for every geometry and salt mixture.
The planar coupling parameter is a declared standard-model definition; the cited current interface/slab papers provide context, not a verified original derivation of this parameter.
Strong coupling between two mechanical modes in the Casimir paper is a different dimensionless comparison from this counterion Xi; matching terminology is not a shared physical mechanism.

nodes.title: Compact and diffuse capacitances in series
nodes.plain: Voltage partition between compact and diffuse layers must be separated before interpreting a measured differential capacitance.
conditions: Uniform planar interface with same incremental charge through both idealized layers; adsorption can introduce additional coupled state variables.
derivation: Write dV=dVS+dVD.
Divide by dSigma and identify the inverse slopes.
limitingCases: The smaller positive capacitance dominates.
pitfalls: A fitted Stern thickness is not necessarily a literal ion diameter or a directly measured molecular boundary.

nodes.title: Acid-site charge regulation
nodes.plain: A surface boundary charge may be an equilibrium unknown rather than a fixed number.

variables.meaning: site equilibrium constant in pH notation

conditions: Independent identical acid sites AH→A−+H+, ideal local proton activity and electrochemical equilibrium; no lateral cooperativity.
derivation: Mass action gives theta/(1−theta)=Ka/aH(surface).
Positive surface potential reduces local proton concentration by exp(−eψ/kBT).
limitingCases: Very low bulk pH protonates the sites under these assumptions.
pitfalls: pH is an activity convention, not simply number density; a sign error reverses the predicted feedback.

nodes.title: Quantum capacitance from compressibility
nodes.plain: Charging a low-density-of-states electron system changes its chemical potential as well as its electrostatic potential.

variables.meaning: density of states per area per joule

conditions: Equilibrium electronic compressibility; integral form assumes an independently specified DOS and no additional self-consistent interaction correction.
derivation: An electrical voltage increment shifts electron electrochemical energy by e*dV.
Differentiate charge density e*n with respect to that increment.

steps: Integrating the normalized Fermi derivative gives1.
workedExample.result: cQ=e²g0, independent of temperature in a broad constant-DOS band.

limitingCases: At zero temperature cQ probes DOS at the chemical potential.
pitfalls: A capacitance fitted from a circuit may also include ions, traps, geometry, kinetics and contacts.

nodes.title: Ideal graphene quantum capacitance
nodes.plain: The clean zero-temperature Dirac model predicts a chemical-potential-dependent electronic capacitance.

variables.meaning: chemical potential measured from Dirac point

conditions: Ideal monolayer graphene with spin/valley degeneracy4, linear dispersion and T=0; disorder/interactions neglected.
derivation: Count2D Dirac states to obtain n=sgn(mu)*mu²/(πhbar²vF²).
Differentiate n with respect to mu and multiply by e².
limitingCases: At ideal T=0 neutrality the formula tends to zero.
pitfalls: Finite temperature and charge puddles smooth the Dirac-point minimum; a real material need not have zero measured capacitance.

nodes.title: Geometric and electronic voltage partition
nodes.plain: Electrochemical charging distributes voltage between the electrostatic gap and electronic compressibility.
conditions: Same incremental areal charge, equilibrium linear response and no unmodeled trap or ionic branch; all areas consistently normalized.
derivation: Total electrochemical voltage is geometric voltage plus chemical-potential change/e.
Differentiate with respect to charge per area.
limitingCases: cQ≫cg recovers the geometric limit.
pitfalls: Negative compressibility can enhance capacitance, but stable total curvature and correct ensemble must still be verified.

nodes.title: Kelvin-probe first-harmonic null
nodes.plain: A force harmonic null estimates a capacitance-weighted contact potential under an instrument model.
conditions: Expand Fz=.5Cprime(z)[Vdc−VCPD+Vac*cos(omega*t)]²; quasistatic capacitive force, fixed tip geometry and uniform effective sample potential.
Coordinate z increases tip–sample separation. With Fz=+Cprime(z)Vgap²/2, Cprime is normally negative for attraction; an opposite coordinate flips force signs but not the null.
derivation: The cross term in squared voltage supplies the omega harmonic.
Its null gives Vdc=VCPD when additional charge forces are absent.

workedExample.result: First harmonic is zero even though DC and2omega forces may remain.

limitingCases: If Vac=0 there is no lock-in harmonic with which to locate the null.
pitfalls: Tip convolution, trapped charge, surface dipoles and feedback dynamics prevent an automatic absolute work-function interpretation.
This first-harmonic identity is derived here from the capacitive-force model; a complete contemporary KPFM instrument review was not performed.
The1991 paper was inspected only through metadata/deposited abstract; do not label this force identity as a checked transcription of that original article.

nodes.title: Thermal charge fluctuations at fixed voltage
nodes.plain: Response and equilibrium noise are linked only within a specified stable ensemble.

variables.meaning: positive differential capacitance at fixed control conditions

conditions: Classical equilibrium, voltage-controlled conjugate ensemble, local convex free energy; low-frequency thermodynamic fluctuations not a full detector noise spectrum.
derivation: Differentiate the voltage-ensemble partition function.
The response derivative equals beta times charge variance.
limitingCases: At strictly fixed total Q that constrained charge has zero ensemble variance.
pitfalls: A negative variance cannot be inferred by substituting an unstable isolated negative capacitance branch.

nodes.title: Electrostatic zero-frequency interaction sector
nodes.plain: This is one classical electrostatic sector of planar fluctuation theory, not the whole retarded quantum Casimir force.

variables.meaning: dimensionless substitution2ka used in the derivation
Riemann zeta value sum of reciprocal positive cubes

conditions: Planar local media with static electric response, equilibrium and specified intervening medium; screening and boundary prescriptions can change the zero mode.
derivation: At zero Matsubara frequency, retain only the static electric/TM sector of the declared planar model. The half-weight zero term times the2D mode measure gives kBT/(4π) times integral k*dk.
Set u=2ka, so k*dk=u*du/(4a²). Expand log(1−exp(−u))=−sum exp(−n*u)/n.
Termwise integration gives integral u*log(1−exp(−u))du=−sum1/n³=−zeta(3); hence one ideal electric sector yields−zeta(3)kBT/(16πa²).

steps: Expand log(1−x) and integrate each exponential term.

limitingCases: If one electric reflection coefficient is zero this sector vanishes.
pitfalls: Adding this term to a full Lifshitz calculation that already includes n=0 double counts it; quantum/retarded sectors are not derived here.
Adding an ideal TE zero mode doubles this term; that is a different magnetic/material boundary prescription, not the single electrostatic sector stated here.

nodes.title: Weak Poisson form with explicit flux sign
nodes.plain: The Neumann variable g is minus the outward displacement flux because E=−gradphi.

variables.meaning: Dirichlet portion where test functions vanish

conditions: Trial potential has specified Dirichlet trace; test functions vanish there; coercivity and integrable sources required.

For the pure-Neumann problem on each connected component, integral rho_f dV + integral g dA=0. Fix the mean or a reference; incompatible data must be rejected rather than hidden by pinning one mesh node.
derivation: Multiply −div(epsilon*gradphi)=rho by v.
Integrate by parts and move the boundary derivative to the right.
limitingCases: For homogeneous Dirichlet data the boundary integral disappears.
pitfalls: Assigning g=D·n reverses the physical sign unless the weak-form convention is changed.

nodes.title: Variational Poisson functional
nodes.plain: Stationarity yields the weak PDE under fixed admissible boundary traces.
conditions: Linear coercive dielectric and fixed sources/boundary controls; gauge fixed for all-Neumann cases.
derivation: Vary phi by a test function.
Set first variation to zero; positivity gives the minimizing solution.

steps: Differentiate J with respect to each coefficient.
workedExample.result: The symmetric stiffness system K*u=f is obtained.

limitingCases: Mesh refinement of a conforming space reduces the functional toward its exact minimum.
pitfalls: This source-loaded PDE functional is not automatically the complete thermodynamic energy of a voltage-controlled mechanical apparatus.

nodes.title: Green boundary representation
nodes.plain: Boundary data can replace a volume discretization in homogeneous regions.
conditions: x strictly inside a smooth bounded homogeneous region; boundary limits require jump terms; kernel solves−LaplacianG=delta.
derivation: Apply Green second identity to phi and G.
Use Poisson and the delta property of G with consistent signs.

workedExample.inputs: Harmonic constant potential V0 inside a sphere
steps: Volume term vanishes; the double-layer integral reproduces the constant.
workedExample.result: Interior phi=V0; evaluating directly on the boundary requires its jump convention.

limitingCases: For a source-free region only boundary terms remain.
pitfalls: Dropping the boundary jump coefficient or using a homogeneous kernel across heterogeneous bulk epsilon gives a wrong integral equation.

nodes.title: Ewald screening split
nodes.plain: An exact algebraic split organizes a long-range periodic sum; it is not by itself the complete periodic energy.
conditions: Identity holds for r>0; full Ewald algorithms additionally require reciprocal terms, self correction, net-charge treatment and a zero-mode/boundary convention.
derivation: Insert erf+erfc=1.
Choose eta so both real and reciprocal representations converge efficiently.
limitingCases: Exact total results must be independent of eta after convergence.
pitfalls: Slab and3D periodic boundaries are different problems; omitting the self term or neutralizing-background convention changes the result.

nodes.title: Tikhonov inverse and a kernel witness
nodes.plain: A regularizer selects a stable estimate under a declared prior; it does not manufacture missing information.

variables.meaning: regularization strength in declared scaled coordinates

conditions: Finite linearized inverse model with consistent nondimensionalization; W positive; combined operator invertible on constrained unknowns.
derivation: Minimize weighted data residual squared plus lambda times penalty squared.
Set its derivative to zero to obtain normal equations.

workedExample.result: x=(1/2,1/2) is a prior-selected representative, not unique recovery from data.

limitingCases: As lambda→0 a unique well-conditioned full-rank inverse is recovered when it exists.
pitfalls: A small residual, positive returned singular values of a rectangular matrix, or a plausible image does not remove an unobserved kernel.

nodes.title: Covariance-aware uncertainty propagation
nodes.plain: A derived result inherits covariance as well as individual input uncertainties.

variables.meaning: input quantities with separately stated units

conditions: Differentiable local measurement model and small enough uncertainties for first-order propagation; coverage probabilities require additional distributional/effective-DOF assumptions.
derivation: Linearize delta y≈sum(Ji*delta xi).
Take its variance, retaining cross terms.

workedExample.inputs: C=Q/V;Q,V have equal1% relative standard uncertainty
steps: For independent errors, add squared sensitivities.
For perfectly common fractional calibration error the correlated terms cancel.
workedExample.result: Independent relative uC≈1.414%; common multiplicative error can cancel exactly in the ratio.

limitingCases: A zero sensitivity suppresses the corresponding first-order contribution, not necessarily higher-order error.
pitfalls: Multiplying by k=2 is not automatically a valid95% interval, and a nonsignificant difference is not equivalence.

Magnetism: fields, matter and controlled inference
nodes.summary: A multiscale map from current-generated fields to quantum materials, spin transport and calibrated measurement. Physical mechanisms and evidence status remain separate.

nodes.title: Classical magnetic fields
nodes.summary: Currents, flux continuity, potentials and boundary-value problems.

nodes.title: Induction and electromagnetic energy
nodes.summary: Time-dependent fields, motional circuits, local energy transfer and passive device budgets.

nodes.title: Magnetic order and material response
nodes.summary: Response functions and microscopic interactions connect atomic moments to domains and phases.

nodes.title: Low-dimensional and moiré magnets
nodes.summary: Dimensionality, anisotropy, stacking and correlations control order and textures.

nodes.title: Spin transport and magnetic dynamics
nodes.summary: Angular momentum transfer, resonances, textures and wave-based information processing.

nodes.title: Superconducting magnetic response
nodes.summary: Equilibrium flux exclusion, screening currents, vortices and critical scales.

nodes.title: Magnetoelectric and hybrid systems
nodes.summary: Cross responses need conjugate variables, symmetry and an external energy supply.

nodes.title: Magnetometry and inverse inference
nodes.summary: Measurements require channel models, geometry, calibration and identifiable source parameters.

nodes.title: Computational magnetism
nodes.summary: Discretization, energy functionals, verification, uncertainty and reproducibility.

nodes.title: Flux density and field intensity
nodes.summary: B describes magnetic induction; H separates free current from macroscopic magnetization. Neither can be replaced by the other without a constitutive statement.

nodes.title: Current distributions
nodes.summary: Line, surface and volume current idealizations have different supports and units.

nodes.title: Steady current kernels
nodes.summary: Magnetostatics assumes stationary sources with consistent return currents.

nodes.title: Biot–Savart reconstruction
nodes.summary: The vector kernel weights each source element by orientation and distance; near-wire singularities reveal the idealization.

nodes.title: Straight-wire symmetry
nodes.summary: An infinitely long thin wire permits a closed-form azimuthal field; finite leads break that symmetry.

nodes.title: Current-loop geometry
nodes.summary: Axial loop fields provide a controlled route from a finite circuit to the far-field dipole.

nodes.title: Ampèrian integral methods
nodes.summary: An integral law is always valid in its domain but solves a field only when symmetry controls the integrand.

nodes.title: Solenoids and return flux
nodes.summary: Long-coil interior estimates omit fringe fields and winding resistance.

nodes.title: Vector potential and gauge
nodes.summary: A curl representation enforces flux continuity; gauge choice does not change B.

nodes.title: Magnetic dipoles and force
nodes.summary: Dipole approximations require source-target separation large relative to source extent.

nodes.title: Bound versus free current
nodes.summary: Magnetization produces volume curl and surface cross-product currents; classifications depend on material coarse graining.

nodes.title: Interface boundary conditions
nodes.summary: Normal B continuity and tangential H jumps encode flux conservation and free surface current.

nodes.title: Faraday induction
nodes.summary: Changing flux and moving material circuits contribute to the same oriented emf.

nodes.title: Motional electromagnetic circuits
nodes.summary: The velocity in a circuit emf is the velocity of the material boundary, not a guessed wave velocity.

nodes.title: Displacement current
nodes.summary: A changing electric displacement repairs continuity and enables waves; quasistatics needs a scale argument.

nodes.title: Local energy accounting
nodes.summary: Poynting flux, storage and mechanical/Joule work identify where supplied energy goes.

nodes.title: Passive ports and finite time
nodes.summary: Initial stored energy and all powered auxiliary ports belong in a finite-window budget.

nodes.title: Hysteretic losses
nodes.summary: A loop measures cycle work only for declared field variables, sample volume and measurement conditions.

nodes.title: Eddy currents and skin effect
nodes.summary: Diffusion and conductive loss can shift response peaks without adding an energy source.

nodes.title: Macroscopic susceptibility
nodes.summary: A scalar constant susceptibility is a restricted linear, reversible approximation.

nodes.title: Demagnetizing fields
nodes.summary: Applied and internal fields differ; ellipsoids supply a special uniform-field solution.

nodes.title: Thermal paramagnetism
nodes.summary: Independent moments give a high-temperature weak-field Curie law, not a universal low-temperature law.

nodes.title: Microscopic exchange
nodes.summary: An effective spin Hamiltonian represents electronic exchange after model reduction.

nodes.title: Ordered phases
nodes.summary: An order parameter and symmetry specify a phase more precisely than the presence of a magnetic signal.

nodes.title: Ferromagnetism
nodes.summary: Parallel order can form domains that hide a large local moment behind small net magnetization.

nodes.title: Domains and walls
nodes.summary: Exchange, anisotropy and magnetostatics compete to set walls and domain patterns.

nodes.title: Continuum wall profiles
nodes.summary: A one-dimensional wall width follows from a specific functional and boundary states.

nodes.title: Antiferromagnetism
nodes.summary: Opposing sublattice moments require a Néel order parameter, not just net M.

nodes.title: Ferrimagnetism and compensation
nodes.summary: Unequal sublattices can compensate net magnetization or angular momentum at different temperatures.

nodes.title: Frustrated interactions
nodes.summary: Not all preferred pairwise alignments can be simultaneously realized on a frustrated lattice.

nodes.title: Quantum spin liquids
nodes.summary: Absence of conventional order alone is insufficient; competing states and disorder must be tested.

nodes.title: Altermagnetic symmetry
nodes.summary: Some compensated collinear orders allow momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting.

nodes.title: Material-specific RuO2 controversy
nodes.summary: Bulk magnetic order, thin-film structure, spin/orbital conversion and interfacial effects are separate claims.

nodes.title: Criticality and finite-size scaling
nodes.summary: Apparent transitions in finite systems require size, dimensionality and dynamical-time analysis.

nodes.title: Two-dimensional order
nodes.summary: Continuous spin symmetry and short-range interactions restrict finite-temperature order; anisotropy changes the premises.

nodes.title: van der Waals layers
nodes.summary: Weak interlayer bonding permits assembly but does not make exchange or disorder negligible.

nodes.title: Twist and stacking
nodes.summary: Twist changes local registry and therefore exchange, anisotropy and relaxation.

nodes.title: Moiré supercell phase coexistence
nodes.summary: Spatially separated local phases and transition scales need resolved measurement rather than one averaged moment.

nodes.title: Electrostatic tuning of magnets
nodes.summary: A gate can alter carriers, electric field and strain; these mechanisms must be discriminated.

nodes.title: Spin–valley correlations
nodes.summary: Valley labels are electronic momentum-space degrees of freedom, not real-space locations.

nodes.title: Magnetic parent states and pairing
nodes.summary: Field-enhanced superconductivity and valley imbalance constrain mechanisms without proving one unique pairing theory.

nodes.title: Magnetization dynamics
nodes.summary: The sign convention for gyromagnetic ratio and choice of B or H must be explicit.

nodes.title: Ferromagnetic resonance
nodes.summary: A resonance depends on effective-field curvature, damping, geometry and drive/readout channels.

nodes.title: Magnonics
nodes.summary: Spin waves carry energy and angular momentum; excitation, propagation and detection losses remain.

nodes.title: Exchange-dominated dispersion
nodes.summary: A quadratic wavevector term is a limiting continuum result, not every film mode dispersion.

nodes.title: Spin and orbital transport
nodes.summary: Spin, orbital and charge currents have distinct units and conversion mechanisms.

nodes.title: Spin Hall conversion
nodes.summary: A conversion angle is defined only after specifying current normalization and geometry.

nodes.title: Spin–orbit torque switching
nodes.summary: Coherent torque, heating and field-induced switching require separate controls.

nodes.title: Chiral textures
nodes.summary: DMI, exchange, anisotropy and dipolar energy stabilize or destabilize different textures.

nodes.title: Skyrmions and topological charge
nodes.summary: A continuum integer invariant requires smoothness and a compactified or fixed boundary.

nodes.title: Optical writing of magnetic textures
nodes.summary: Laser pulses are an external energy input; field-free is not energy-free.

nodes.title: Ultrafast Néel dynamics
nodes.summary: Two-sublattice exchange gives dynamics not captured by a single ferromagnetic macrospin.

nodes.title: Meissner equilibrium response
nodes.summary: Equilibrium flux expulsion differs from frozen flux in an ideal perfect conductor.

nodes.title: London screening
nodes.summary: A local homogeneous superfluid model gives exponential screening only in a stated geometry.

nodes.title: Fluxoid and phase winding
nodes.summary: Phase single-valuedness constrains a fluxoid; magnetic flux alone needs additional limits.

nodes.title: Type-II vortices
nodes.summary: Vortex cores, penetration depth and sample geometry distinguish lower and upper critical fields.

nodes.title: Ginzburg–Landau description
nodes.summary: A coarse-grained order parameter has a controlled near-transition regime, not unrestricted microscopic authority.

nodes.title: Magnet–superconductor hybrids
nodes.summary: Stray fields, screening, proximity and dissipation couple distinct subsystems.

nodes.title: Cross-response thermodynamics
nodes.summary: A derivative with respect to H differs by permeability factors from one with respect to B.

nodes.title: Linear magnetoelectric tensor
nodes.summary: Symmetry and chosen thermodynamic potential determine allowed reciprocal cross responses.

nodes.title: Layer-resolved orbital response
nodes.summary: A bilayer layer-pseudospin response is not automatically the bulk SI magnetoelectric coefficient.

nodes.title: Magnetoelastic transduction
nodes.summary: Changing strain can modify anisotropy; external electrical/mechanical work remains in the budget.

nodes.title: Cavity and resonator hybrids
nodes.summary: Avoided crossing alone does not establish a useful autonomous energy source or quantum advantage.

nodes.title: Sensor transfer functions
nodes.summary: A magnetometer produces a calibrated channel with finite bandwidth, orientation and noise.

nodes.title: NV-center magnetometry
nodes.summary: Zeeman shifts depend on the projection along a known crystallographic axis and the applicable spin Hamiltonian.

nodes.title: Hall and inductive probes
nodes.summary: Hall voltage and pickup-coil emf measure different functions of the same field history.

nodes.title: Measurement uncertainty
nodes.summary: Calibration, correlation, geometry and drift can dominate counting noise.

nodes.title: Inverse magnetization
nodes.summary: External fields need not uniquely determine a vector magnetization distribution.

nodes.title: Height continuation and bandwidth
nodes.summary: High-spatial-frequency components decay rapidly above the sample and amplify noise on inversion.

nodes.title: Magnetic inverse null spaces
nodes.summary: A single field component generally cannot identify every source component without extra assumptions.

nodes.title: Physics-informed reconstruction
nodes.summary: A fitted field can coexist with multiple magnetization explanations; priors and held-out data must be reported.

nodes.title: Micromagnetic energy functionals
nodes.summary: A continuous unit-vector model excludes atomic-scale degrees of freedom by construction.

nodes.title: Mesh and timestep convergence
nodes.summary: Agreement at one grid spacing is not convergence; resolve relevant exchange and wall scales.

nodes.title: Exchange functional
nodes.summary: Gradient penalties approximate slowly varying exchange and need compatible boundary conditions.

nodes.title: Anisotropy functional
nodes.summary: Easy axes and energy offsets must be stated with the coefficient convention.

nodes.title: DMI conventions and boundaries
nodes.summary: Bulk and interfacial DMI have different invariant forms and boundary twists.

nodes.title: Code verification versus validation
nodes.summary: Analytic/standard-problem agreement verifies implementation within a model, not actual material parameters.

nodes.title: MuMax3 verification corpus
nodes.summary: Selected source sections expose finite-difference approximations and even benchmark disagreement.

nodes.title: Electronic-structure model choices
nodes.summary: Exchange-correlation approximations and Hubbard U can change predicted magnetic ground states.

nodes.title: Reproducibility and uncertainty
nodes.summary: Record code/version, mesh, convergence, material parameters, boundary conditions and numerical budgets.

nodes.title: Magnetic flux continuity
nodes.plain: Divergence-free B has zero net outward flux through a closed surface.
conditions: Classical Maxwell theory with no magnetic monopoles; include all faces of a closed surface.
derivation: Apply the divergence theorem to local flux continuity.
Opposite face contributions cancel for a uniform field.

steps: Top flux=+0.0001 Wb; bottom=-0.0001 Wb; sides zero.

limitingCases: A nonzero open-surface flux is entirely compatible.
pitfalls: Zero divergence does not imply zero curl or zero local field.

nodes.title: Biot–Savart law for a filament
nodes.latex: \mathbf B(\mathbf r)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int \frac{d\boldsymbol\ell\times(\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime)}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r^\prime|^3}
nodes.plain: Sum oriented steady-current elements using the inverse-distance vector kernel.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
oriented line element in current direction

conditions: Steady localized current with a physically completed return path; vacuum.
Observation point is outside the ideal filament.
derivation: Solve the vector Poisson equation in Coulomb gauge with the free-space Green function.
Take its curl to obtain the cross-product kernel.

workedExample.inputs: Circular loop I=1 A, R=0.1 m; evaluate centre
steps: All axial contributions add; transverse contributions cancel.
Integrate circumference to obtain mu0 I/(2R).

limitingCases: The far field of a localized closed loop is dipolar, not an isolated-wire 1/r field.
pitfalls: Do not omit return current when predicting a finite device field.

nodes.title: Infinite straight wire
nodes.plain: Cylindrical symmetry turns Ampere circulation into an azimuthal field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Infinite thin wire, vacuum, stationary current; r exceeds conductor radius.
derivation: Choose a coaxial circular contour.
B is tangential and constant on the contour, so 2 pi r B=mu0 I.
limitingCases: As I tends to zero, B vanishes; the singular r→0 limit is outside the thin-wire domain.
pitfalls: A finite wire cannot inherit this expression arbitrarily close to its ends.

nodes.title: On-axis circular-loop field
nodes.plain: The axial field of a thin circular loop interpolates between centre field and a dipole.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Circular filament in vacuum; observation on its symmetry axis.
derivation: Project the Biot–Savart cross product onto the axis.
The denominator is constant around the loop; integrate azimuth.
limitingCases: At z=0 recover mu0 I/(2R); for |z|≫R recover z^-3.
pitfalls: The expression is not the off-axis field of a finite solenoid.

nodes.title: Magnetostatic free-current circulation
nodes.plain: H circulation counts free current after magnetization is separated out.
conditions: Stationary fields; displacement current negligible; contour and normal follow right-hand orientation.
derivation: Apply Stokes theorem to curl H=Jf.
Integrate current density over the spanning surface.

workedExample.inputs: Ienc=3 A; circular contour radius=0.1 m with cylindrical symmetry

limitingCases: Zero enclosed current gives zero circulation, not necessarily H=0 everywhere.
pitfalls: Ampere law does not justify constant H on a nonsymmetric contour.

nodes.title: Long-solenoid interior estimate
nodes.plain: Turns per unit length set the ideal long air-core coil field.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Length much larger than radius, observation away from ends, air core, negligible winding thickness.
derivation: Choose an Ampere rectangle along the interior and remote exterior.
Neglect exterior contribution and count n*l turns.
limitingCases: At an ideal long coil end the on-axis field is about half the deep-interior value.
pitfalls: Real coil heating, fringe fields and magnetic core saturation are separate calculations.

nodes.title: Macroscopic B–H–M relation
nodes.plain: Magnetization is magnetic moment per material volume; the relation defines H in SI.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Macroscopic SI fields defined at compatible coarse-graining scale.
derivation: Separate microscopic current into free and magnetization contributions.
Define H=B/mu0−M; no linear material law is assumed.

workedExample.inputs: Collinear H=100 A/m and M=900 A/m

limitingCases: For M=0, vacuum B=mu0 H; at H=0 an ordered sample can have M≠0.
pitfalls: B and H do not have the same SI units; B=mu H additionally assumes a constitutive law.

nodes.title: Volume magnetization current
nodes.plain: Spatially varying magnetization has an equivalent bound volume current.
conditions: Continuum magnetization differentiable inside the material; add interface surface currents separately.
derivation: Represent localized magnetic moments as small current loops.
Interior loop contributions cancel except where magnetization varies.
limitingCases: Uniform M has zero volume curl but generally nonzero surface current.
pitfalls: Zero Jb in the bulk does not imply an unmagnetized body.

nodes.title: Surface magnetization current
nodes.plain: The boundary current closes magnetization loops at an interface.
conditions: Use the magnetization jump if both sides are magnetic; orientation is outward from the chosen body.
derivation: Integrate volume curl through an infinitesimal interface layer.
The normal derivative of the magnetization step produces a surface sheet.
limitingCases: A face normal parallel to M carries no equivalent surface current.
pitfalls: The order M cross n matters; reversing it reverses circulation.

nodes.title: Far-field magnetic dipole
nodes.latex: \mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r^3}[3(\mathbf m\cdot\hat{\mathbf r})\hat{\mathbf r}-\mathbf m]
nodes.plain: A localized current distribution has a leading magnetic dipole term.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: r much larger than source extent; outside the source in vacuum.
derivation: Expand the localized vector potential at large distance.
The closed-current monopole term vanishes; curl the leading moment term.

workedExample.inputs: m=0.1 A m²; axial r=0.1 m

limitingCases: At the equator the field points opposite m with half the axial magnitude.
pitfalls: The singular point-dipole field cannot describe the source interior.

nodes.title: Dipole torque and energy
nodes.plain: A fixed permanent dipole tends to align with the applied field.
conditions: Small fixed moment in a field uniform over the dipole; induced moments require material work accounting.
derivation: Sum Lorentz forces around a small loop.
Integrate torque against angle to obtain U=−mB cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: m=0.01 A m²; B=0.1 T; perpendicular orientation
workedExample.result: Torque=0.001 N m; aligned U=−0.001 J

limitingCases: Aligned torque is zero although energy is minimal, not zero by necessity.
pitfalls: An induced moment may introduce a factor1/2 in energy after its formation is included.

nodes.title: Force on a fixed dipole
nodes.plain: The gradient of dipole potential gives force when its moment is fixed.
conditions: Small rigid moment, quasistatic external field, derivatives at fixed m.
derivation: Use F=−gradient U with U=−m dot B.
Keep self field and induced-response work outside this simplified potential.

steps: Multiply mz by axial field gradient.

limitingCases: A uniform field can exert torque but gives no translational dipole force.
pitfalls: A field magnitude alone is insufficient to determine lifting force.

nodes.title: Magnetic flux
nodes.plain: Flux is the oriented surface integral, not B multiplied by any convenient area.

variables.meaning: magnetic flux through chosen oriented surface

conditions: A defined surface and normal; B and geometry may vary across it.
derivation: Sum infinitesimal normal field contributions.
For a uniform field and flat area, obtain BA cos(theta).

workedExample.inputs: B=0.2 T; A=0.01 m²; field at60degrees to normal

limitingCases: A surface parallel to field has zero flux despite nonzero B.
pitfalls: Angle is measured from the normal, not from the surface plane.

nodes.title: Oriented moving-loop Faraday law
nodes.plain: Electric and motional contributions give the emf around the actual moving material loop.
conditions: A well-defined material circuit and right-hand orientation; ideal thin circuit approximation.
derivation: Combine local curl E=−partial B/partial t with the moving-surface transport theorem.
The boundary motion term is v cross B, not an extra energy source.

workedExample.inputs: Stationary loop, flux rises by0.003 Wb over0.1 s
workedExample.result: emf=−0.03 V for the chosen positive circulation

limitingCases: Steady B can induce emf if the loop area/orientation changes.
pitfalls: Reversing the chosen normal reverses both flux and emf sign consistently.

nodes.title: Ampère–Maxwell law
nodes.plain: Free current and displacement-current density both source the curl of H.
conditions: Macroscopic Maxwell equations with polarization placed in D.
derivation: Add displacement current to preserve free-charge continuity.
Taking divergence gives divergence Jf+partial rho_f/partial t=0 using divergence D=rho_f.

workedExample.inputs: Charging capacitor: dD/dt=2 A/m² over0.01 m²
steps: Integrate displacement current density over gap area.

limitingCases: The term may be negligible in a specific MQS limit, not identically absent.
pitfalls: Displacement current is not a flow of free charges across an ideal vacuum capacitor gap.

nodes.title: Vacuum Poynting theorem
nodes.latex: \partial_t u+\nabla\cdot\mathbf S=-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf E,\quad\mathbf S=\mathbf E\times\mathbf H
nodes.plain: Field storage plus outward electromagnetic flux equals negative work rate on matter.
conditions: Vacuum fields with material currents treated explicitly; material storage needs a consistent constitutive energy model.
derivation: Dot Ampère–Maxwell with E and Faraday with H.
Subtract using divergence(E cross H)=H dot curl E−E dot curl H.

workedExample.inputs: Control volume: inward flux3 W; stored-energy rise1 W
steps: Outward integrated S=−3 W; dU/dt=1 W.

limitingCases: A steady state can have nonzero energy flux while storage is constant.
pitfalls: Field enhancement is not net output; include every boundary port and initial storage.

nodes.title: Vacuum field-energy density
nodes.plain: Quadratic vacuum storage follows from reversible field work.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Vacuum or a specified linear nondispersive analogue; not a general hysteretic-material formula.
derivation: Integrate E dD and H dB along a reversible constitutive path.
In vacuum D=epsilon0 E and H=B/mu0.

workedExample.inputs: E=0; B=0.01 T in volume0.001 m³

limitingCases: Storage vanishes quadratically as B→0.
pitfalls: Using B²/(2mu) in a nonlinear hysteretic core can give incorrect material energy accounting.

nodes.title: Passive inductor and winding budget
nodes.plain: Source power splits into changing magnetic storage and nonnegative winding dissipation.
conditions: L positive and constant, R≥0, no additional coupled or powered ports.
derivation: Multiply voltage equation by current.
Use L i di/dt=d(Li²/2)/dt.

workedExample.inputs: L=0.1 H; i rises0→2 A; R=0 for illustrative storage
workedExample.result: Input work=0.2 J; no continuous output from a fixed stored state

limitingCases: With source off, a resistor can drain initial energy but cannot replenish it.
pitfalls: A changing L introduces mechanical/coupling work; do not omit it.

nodes.title: Cycle work in magnetic material
nodes.plain: An oriented quasistatic B–H loop gives magnetic work per sample volume for a completed cycle.

variables.meaning: net supplied work per cycle per volume

conditions: Closed periodic cycle, consistent internal field and sample volume; separate nonmagnetic apparatus losses.
derivation: Integrate local magnetic work H dot dB.
Reversible storage returns to its initial value after a cycle, leaving net dissipative work.

workedExample.inputs: Rectangular scalar loop: coercive Hc=100 A/m; remanent Br=0.5 T
workedExample.result: Dissipated work=200 J/m³ per cycle under this loop idealization

limitingCases: A reversible single-valued path traversed forward and back encloses zero area.
pitfalls: A counterclockwise plotted loop may change algebraic sign; passivity uses work supplied to matter.

nodes.title: Ellipsoidal internal-field correction
nodes.plain: A uniform ellipsoid gives a closed correction for reversible scalar susceptibility.
conditions: Uniform ellipsoid, principal-axis drive, linear reversible medium; SI factors sum to1.
derivation: Combine demagnetizing field −NM with M=chi Hint.
Solve the one-variable linear equation for M.
limitingCases: For chi→0, M≈chi Happ; large chi is shape-limited.
pitfalls: CGS demagnetizing factors can sum to4pi; do not mix conventions.

nodes.title: Weak-field Curie susceptibility
nodes.plain: Independent isotropically orientable moments respond linearly when thermal energy dominates alignment.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Noninteracting moments in weak field mu B≪kB T; classical orientation or appropriate quantum effective moment.
derivation: For classical isotropic independent moments use x=mu B/(kB T) and Z_orientation=4pi sinh(x)/x. Its mean axial moment is mu[coth(x)−1/x].
Expand coth(x)−1/x=x/3+O(x³), multiply by number density, and use B≈mu0 H in this weak-response limit. This is an explanatory derivation, distinct from the source’s two-state Ising normalization.
limitingCases: The expression cannot be extrapolated to T=0 or saturation.
pitfalls: It is not a ferromagnetic hysteresis law and does not include exchange correlations.
An Ising two-state moment has a different weak-field angular factor; do not import its normalized B coupling as SI tesla.

nodes.title: Curie–Weiss phenomenology
nodes.plain: A molecular-field correction shifts the Curie-law denominator.
conditions: Paramagnetic regime sufficiently far from transitions; fitted C and theta are model-dependent.
derivation: Assume an effective field H+lambda M and insert the Curie response.
Solve for M/H and absorb molecular-field coefficient into theta.

workedExample.inputs: C=0.1 K; T=300 K; theta=50 K

limitingCases: theta=0 recovers Curie behavior; the denominator divergence is not a literal finite-sample infinity.
pitfalls: Negative theta suggests dominant AFM correlations, not proof of a spin liquid or an ordering temperature.

nodes.title: Heisenberg exchange convention
nodes.plain: With this plus-sign convention, positive J favors antiparallel spin correlations.

variables.meaning: dimensionless spin operator at site i

conditions: Specify lattice, spin magnitude, boundary and omitted anisotropy/dipolar terms.
derivation: Reduce an electronic low-energy problem to spin degrees of freedom under declared assumptions.
For two spin1/2 particles, S1 dot S2 has eigenvalues−3/4 and+1/4.
limitingCases: For J<0 the triplet is lower in this convention.
pitfalls: Some authors write−J S dot S and reverse the meaning of positive J.

nodes.title: Classical triangular AFM counterexample
nodes.latex: E=J(\mathbf s_1\cdot\mathbf s_2+\mathbf s_2\cdot\mathbf s_3+\mathbf s_3\cdot\mathbf s_1)
nodes.plain: Three unit spins cannot make all three AFM bonds antiparallel.
conditions: Classical isotropic spins on a single triangular plaquette, zero field.
derivation: Write E=J(|s1+s2+s3|²−3)/2.
The lower bound occurs when the three vectors sum to zero.

workedExample.result: Emin=−1.5 J rather than the impossible−3 J

limitingCases: The 120degree classical ground state is ordered; frustration alone is not a quantum-spin-liquid proof.
pitfalls: Do not transfer a three-site classical minimum to an infinite quantum lattice without analysis.

nodes.title: Gilbert dynamics with positive gamma convention
nodes.latex: \dot{\mathbf m}=-\frac{\gamma}{1+\alpha^2}[\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff}+\alpha\mathbf m\times(\mathbf m\times\mathbf B_{eff})]
nodes.plain: A unit magnetization precesses and damps with a declared positive gyromagnetic magnitude.

variables.meaning: effective induction including selected energy terms

conditions: Fixed saturation magnitude; differentiable effective energy; torque sources and temperature terms must be added explicitly.
derivation: Solve Gilbert implicit equation dm/dt=−gamma m cross B+alpha m cross dm/dt.
Use m dot dm/dt=0 to invert its tangent-plane operator.

workedExample.inputs: alpha=0; Bz=0.1 T; gamma=1.760e11 rad/(T s)
steps: Angular rate=gamma B=1.760e10 rad/s; divide by2pi.

limitingCases: With alpha=0 and static energy, precession conserves energy; alpha>0 removes energy for the consistent convention.
pitfalls: The selected MuMax paper prints a plus-prefactor gamma_LL form; this entry chooses positive gamma and an explicit minus sign. Check the source convention and actual precession direction before converting symbols.

nodes.title: Continuum exchange energy and effective field
nodes.plain: A smooth magnetization texture costs gradient energy and creates a restoring exchange field.
conditions: Constant A and Ms; slowly varying texture; appropriate fixed or natural boundaries.
derivation: Vary the gradient functional and integrate by parts.
Use Beff=−(1/Ms) deltaE/deltam as a volume functional derivative.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; sinusoidal wave k=1e7/m; Ms=8e5 A/m

limitingCases: Uniform m has zero exchange energy in this reference.
pitfalls: A mesh that cannot resolve rotation between cells misrepresents this continuum model.

nodes.title: Uniaxial anisotropy convention
nodes.plain: Positive K in this convention favors alignment along either easy-axis direction.
conditions: One uniaxial contribution with a chosen zero of energy; other anisotropies may coexist.
derivation: Expand a time-reversal-even scalar energy in the axis projection.
Subtract a constant so aligned states have zero energy.

workedExample.inputs: K=1e5 J/m³; m at45degrees to u

limitingCases: Parallel and antiparallel easy-axis states are degenerate under this term alone.
pitfalls: A negative coefficient changes the easy directions; do not infer them from the symbol K alone.

nodes.title: Interfacial DMI energy convention
nodes.plain: An inversion-asymmetric interfacial invariant favors one texture chirality.

variables.meaning: DMI energy per volume in effective thin-film convention

conditions: Thin-film interfacial symmetry; derivatives x,y only; boundary terms and normal orientation matter.
derivation: Construct a scalar linear in gradients allowed by interfacial symmetry.
A functional variation generates a chiral field plus nontrivial boundary conditions.

workedExample.inputs: One-dimensional cycloid m=(sin(qx),0,cos(qx)); q=1e7/m; D=1e-3 J/m²
steps: Substitution gives wD=Dq for this convention.
workedExample.result: wD=1e4 J/m³; reversing q reverses the sign

limitingCases: D=0 restores degeneracy of opposite chiralities for this term.
pitfalls: Bulk D m dot curl m is a different invariant; surface D_s in J/m must be divided by thickness to compare this effective D.

nodes.title: Magnetostatic exchange length
nodes.plain: Exchange and magnetostatic energy density scales define a useful resolution length.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Continuum ferromagnet; a characteristic scale, not a universal sufficient mesh certificate.
derivation: Balance gradient density A/ell² against mu0 Ms²/2.
Solve for ell.
limitingCases: Increasing A broadens the scale; increasing Ms reduces it.
pitfalls: DMI, anisotropy, interfaces and convergence may require smaller cells than this estimate.

nodes.title: Ideal one-dimensional domain wall
nodes.plain: Exchange and positive uniaxial anisotropy set a wall parameter and surface energy.

variables.meaning: wall profile parameter, not necessarily reported full width

conditions: One-dimensional180degree wall, no DMI or nonlocal demagnetizing correction; fixed opposite domains.
derivation: Minimize integral[A(theta prime)²+K sin²theta] dx.
First integral gives A(theta prime)²=K sin²theta; integrate the wall energy.
limitingCases: K→0 broadens the wall and invalidates isolated localized-wall assumptions in a finite sample.
pitfalls: Some papers call pi*Delta the wall width; define the convention before comparison.

nodes.title: Thin-film macrospin resonance
nodes.plain: Two restoring-field curvatures set the in-plane uniform-mode frequency.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
applied induction-equivalent mu0 H in plane
effective magnetization including declared perpendicular anisotropy

conditions: Uniform saturated film, small-angle motion, negligible damping shift; geometry/anisotropy convention specified.
derivation: Linearize torque around the in-plane equilibrium.
Combine two coupled transverse equations to obtain the product of restoring fields.

workedExample.inputs: gamma/(2pi)=28 GHz/T; BH=0.1 T; mu0 Meff=1 T

limitingCases: Setting Meff=0 reduces the expression to the simple Larmor frequency.
pitfalls: Do not insert H in A/m into a formula whose field arguments are tesla.

nodes.title: Exchange-dominated spin-wave limit
nodes.plain: A uniformly magnetized exchange continuum has quadratic wavevector dispersion in this limit.
conditions: Small-amplitude mode, uniform equilibrium, neglect dipolar dispersion/anisotropy or absorb appropriate constants in B0.
derivation: Insert a transverse plane wave into the exchange field.
Linearize undamped LLG to get precession with the shifted restoring field.

workedExample.inputs: A=1e-11 J/m; Ms=8e5 A/m; k=1e7/m; gamma/(2pi)=28 GHz/T

limitingCases: As k→0 the exchange shift vanishes, but other gap terms may remain.
pitfalls: A measured film mode can be dipolar, exchange-dominated or mixed; this is not the entire magnon spectrum.

nodes.title: Skyrmion degree
nodes.plain: An oriented smooth two-dimensional spin texture maps the compactified plane to the unit sphere.
conditions: Fixed common boundary direction or compact domain; no singular point where |m| vanishes.
derivation: Integrate oriented area swept on the unit sphere and normalize by4pi.
For an axisymmetric texture reduce the integral to azimuthal winding and polar endpoint values.

workedExample.inputs: Azimuthal winding n=1; core theta=pi; boundary theta=0
workedExample.result: Q=−1; reversing orientation conventions can reverse its sign

limitingCases: A uniform state has Q=0; a boundary-unfixed partial texture need not give an integer.
pitfalls: Topological charge alone does not guarantee infinite lifetime or free energy; boundaries and singular events permit changes.

nodes.title: Spin Hall normalization
nodes.plain: A declared scalar spin Hall angle relates selected spin-angular-momentum flux to charge current density.

variables.meaning: signed conversion angle for stated axes

conditions: A specified material, transport geometry and spin polarization convention; tensor character suppressed only for one chosen component.
For this scalar example define charge along+x, flux along+z and polarization along+y; the signed thetaSH is defined for exactly that ordered axis choice.
derivation: Express spin flux as angular momentum per transported carrier.
Define thetaSH by the ratio of normalized transverse spin flux to charge flux.

workedExample.result: js=3.29106e-7 J/m² in the angular-momentum-flux convention

limitingCases: Changing spin-flux convention to charge-equivalent A/m² removes the hbar/(2e) prefactor.
pitfalls: A spin current is not an extra source of energy; injector electrical power and interface losses remain.
A spin Hall angle is a normalization-dependent conversion ratio, not an event probability; its magnitude is not universally bounded by1.

nodes.title: Damping-like spin–orbit torque
nodes.plain: A transverse angular-momentum input can reorient an ordered moment.
conditions: A selected torque term in an explicitly powered model; two-sublattice AFMs require the corresponding sublattice torques.
derivation: Resolve the injected spin into the tangent plane perpendicular to m.
Use m cross(s cross m)=s−(m dot s)m.

steps: The tangent direction is zhat; instantaneous rate scale is gamma BDL.
workedExample.result: dm/dt=1.76e8 zhat per second for this isolated term

limitingCases: Collinear s and m give zero torque for this term.
pitfalls: Switching depends on competing fields, pulse shape and heating; a torque expression is not a complete switching prediction.

nodes.title: London penetration in a half-space
nodes.plain: Local superfluid screening produces exponential equilibrium penetration in the simple half-space.
conditions: Static homogeneous London regime, planar surface, weak fields without vortices or strong nonlocality; bulk boundary B→0.
derivation: Combine curl js=−B/(mu0 lambdaL²) with stationary Ampere law and divergence B=0.
Select the decaying solution of the one-dimensional second-order equation.

workedExample.inputs: B(0)=1 mT; lambdaL=100 nm; z=200 nm

limitingCases: The growing exponential is excluded by the bulk boundary condition.
pitfalls: An ideal perfect conductor preserves initial flux; equilibrium Meissner expulsion needs more than infinite DC conductivity.

nodes.title: Superconducting flux quantum and fluxoid
nodes.plain: Single-valued pair phase quantizes a fluxoid, with magnetic flux alone recovered when the current term is negligible.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant

conditions: Closed contour in a coherent superconducting region; conventional2e pairing assumed; finite kinetic-current correction retained.
derivation: Integrate the gauge-invariant phase-gradient relation around a closed loop.
Phase change is2pi n; retain both vector-potential and supercurrent terms.

workedExample.inputs: h=6.62607015e-34 J s; e=1.602176634e-19 C; n=1; negligible current correction

limitingCases: In thin/high-kinetic-inductance loops, flux need not equal nPhi0 even though fluxoid does.
pitfalls: Flux quantization is not a universal quantization of arbitrary classical coil flux.

nodes.title: Ginzburg–Landau scale ratio
nodes.plain: Penetration and coherence scales organize superconducting interfaces and the orbital upper critical field.
conditions: Conventional isotropic GL description near its controlled transition regime; orbital limit, neglect paramagnetic/multiband modifications.
derivation: Nondimensionalize the GL equations by lambda and xi.
Linearized order-parameter onset in a uniform field gives the orbital length condition.

workedExample.inputs: lambda=100 nm; xi=10 nm; Phi0=2.067833848e-15 Wb
workedExample.result: kappa=10; Bc2≈3.29 T in this orbital approximation

limitingCases: The GL interface crossover is kappa=1/sqrt2 under the standard isotropic premises.
pitfalls: A material measured far from Tc may require a microscopic theory; this is not its universal critical field.

These sources support the Landau/phase and flux-quantum ingredients. A direct original GL/Hc2 source was not reviewed; the stated orbital formula is the explanatory linear-GL reconstruction, not a result inferred from the graphene preprint.

nodes.title: SI magnetoelectric cross derivative
nodes.plain: A reciprocal static cross response follows from one explicitly chosen thermodynamic potential.

variables.meaning: vacuum magnetic permeability, measured CODATA constant
linear SI magnetoelectric tensor in this E,H convention

conditions: Equilibrium reversible small-field expansion at fixed declared thermodynamic variables; allowed tensor components depend on symmetry.
derivation: Use dg=−P dot dE−mu0 M dot dH for the selected material contribution.
Differentiate the bilinear cross term and equate mixed derivatives.
limitingCases: A coefficient defined using B or electric displacement instead of H/E has different factors and potentially units.
pitfalls: The layer-pseudospin polarizability in the selected bilayer paper is not silently identified with this bulk SI coefficient.

Only for volumetric M and a fixed uniform constitutive D=epsilon E can alpha_(E,H)=mu0*epsilon*(partial M/partial D). A two-dimensional layer moment may additionally require a thickness normalization; none is silently supplied.

nodes.title: NV axial Zeeman splitting
nodes.plain: A simple axial NV-center model converts a calibrated spin transition shift into a field projection.

variables.meaning: field projection along the known NV axis

conditions: Weak suitably aligned field, negligible transverse mixing/strain or independently calibrated corrections; approximate spin1 Hamiltonian.
derivation: Diagonalize D Sz²+gammae Bparallel Sz/(2pi) in frequency units.
Transition shifts are opposite for the m_s=±1 branches.

workedExample.result: Each branch shifts2.8 MHz; branch separation changes5.6 MHz

limitingCases: Temperature drift in D shifts both branches and can mimic single-line field changes.
pitfalls: One NV axis measures a projection, not an unconstrained three-component vector field.

nodes.title: Stray-field Fourier height filtering
nodes.plain: In a source-free half-space, lateral high-spatial-frequency magnetic structure decays with height.

variables.meaning: lateral Fourier field amplitude under a fixed transform convention

conditions: Planar Fourier analysis in a homogeneous source-free half-space; choose the solution decaying at infinity.
derivation: A scalar magnetic potential satisfies Laplace equation above sources.
Fourier transform laterally to obtain partial_z² potential=|k|² potential.
limitingCases: At k=0 the exponential is1, but boundary/source constraints can make particular uniform channels unobservable.
pitfalls: Exact back-propagation multiplies noise exponentially; regularization adds assumptions, not missing data.

nodes.title: Correlated first-order uncertainty propagation
nodes.plain: A local sensitivity Jacobian propagates a declared input covariance into output variance.

variables.meaning: input covariance, product of input units

conditions: Small enough uncertainties for linearization; covariance and model must be justified independently.
derivation: Taylor-expand output around nominal inputs.
Take variance of the linearized combination, retaining cross terms.

workedExample.inputs: y=x1−x2; each standard uncertainty=1 microtesla; correlationrho=0.9

limitingCases: Perfect common-mode correlation cancels in a difference only for matched sensitivities.
pitfalls: Ignoring covariance can overstate or understate uncertainty; no automatic95percent confidence follows from an arbitrary bound.

nodes.title: Two-dipole observation matrix and an explicit kernel
nodes.plain: A centred Bz measurement cannot distinguish two equally oriented dipoles at mirror-symmetric known positions.

variables.meaning: known dipole forward matrix for specified sensor/source geometry
common knownBz coupling coefficient at a symmetry-axis observation

conditions: Two ideal point dipoles atx=±a,y=z=0 withfixedz orientation;point-dipole far-field premise;known a andsensorheight h.
OneBz channel atx=y=0;the twounknowns are moments,notunknown positions/orientations.
derivation: The vacuum dipole kernel gives c=(mu0/4pi)(2h²−a²)/(a²+h²)^(5/2), wherea,h arelengths inmetres andmu0 isvacuum permeability.
Forc≠0 the1×2operator hasrank1andnullity1:K(1,−1)^T=0 although its onlyreturned singular value issqrt(2)|c|>0.

steps: AddBz atx=0.5m,z=2m:then the2×2matrixdeterminant is1.8688737689e−16[T/(A m²)]²andthe two-moment toy becomesinvertible.
workedExample.result: A singlemeasurement admits(2+t,1−t)for everyt;the off-axis secondmeasurementrecovers(2,1)withfloating errorbelow1e−12 inthis executedexample.

limitingCases: Repeatingcentredmeasurements atthreeheights2,3,4mstillhasrank1andnullity1becauseeachrow retains identicalcolumns.
Choosingh=a/sqrt2makesc=0andthe singleobservationrank0;anunmentionedzero-coupling casewouldinvalidatethe rank1claim.
pitfalls: Full-rank forthe restrictedtwo-moment toydoesnotprove uniquenessofanarbitrarycontinuum vector magnetization.
Invertibility isnot goodnoiseconditioning;report sensitivity,geometryuncertaintyandnoiseafterchoosing measurementunits/scales.
