nodes.title: Newtonian two-body attraction
nodes.plain: The separation vector points from source M to test mass m; the minus sign makes attraction.

variables.meaning: Source-to-test separation vector; scalar r in denominator is its positive Euclidean norm
Newtonian interaction potential energy introduced in derivation

conditions: Point masses or exterior spherical source
Nonrelativistic isolated interaction
derivation: Rotational symmetry fixes a radial force.
Potential U=-GMm/r gives F=-grad U.

steps: The force points toward the source.

limitingCases: M=0 gives zero force
pitfalls: At r=0 the point model is singular; an extended density must replace it.

nodes.title: Acceleration field
nodes.plain: Test-body acceleration is force divided by inertial mass under equality of inertial and passive gravitational mass.

variables.meaning: Separation vector; scalar r in denominator is its positive Euclidean norm

conditions: Test mass does not appreciably perturb source
Universal coupling assumed
derivation: Divide Newton force by m.
The test mass cancels algebraically.
limitingCases: Far from source magnitude tends to zero
pitfalls: Mass cancellation in the model is not an experimental proof of universal free fall.

nodes.title: Potential and conservative acceleration
nodes.plain: Potential is energy per unit test mass, fixed here to zero at infinity.
conditions: Static isolated spherical source
Zero potential at infinity
derivation: Integrate -GM/r² radially with boundary Phi(infinity)=0.
Differentiate to recover acceleration.

steps: Its gradient, not its arbitrary additive constant, affects acceleration.

limitingCases: Adding a constant leaves g unchanged
pitfalls: Do not identify a coordinate potential value with a directly measured absolute energy.

nodes.title: Poisson equation
nodes.plain: Mass density sources a Newtonian potential through a boundary-value problem.
conditions: Newtonian static or instantaneous approximation
Boundary conditions specified
Classical pointwise equation requires sufficient potential/source regularity; point masses and surface layers require a distributional interpretation at the singularsupport.
derivation: Use Gauss divergence theorem with flux integral of g=-4piG enclosed mass.
Set g=-grad Phi.
limitingCases: Vacuum has LaplacianPhi=0, not necessarily zero field
pitfalls: A harmonic potential can be nonzero; source equation without boundaries is not unique.
For Phi=-GM/r, the Laplacian vanishes only off r=0; distributionally it equals4piGM delta3 at the origin. No automaticglobalC2regularity follows from writing the equation.

nodes.title: Escape speed
nodes.plain: Zero energy at infinity determines the ideal minimum launch speed.
conditions: No atmosphere or other bodies
Newtonian point/exterior spherical source
derivation: Set specific energy v²/2-GM/r to zero.
Solve positive speed.
limitingCases: As r increases escape speed decreases
pitfalls: A local escape estimate neglects later thrust, drag and other gravitating bodies.

nodes.title: Circular orbital speed
nodes.plain: Centripetal acceleration equals gravitational acceleration for an ideal circular orbit.
conditions: Test-body circular orbit
Newtonian weak field
derivation: Set v²/r=GM/r².
Take positive magnitude.

steps: Compare escape speed at the same radius.

limitingCases: v_esc=sqrt2 v_c
pitfalls: Using altitude as radius instead of centre distance produces a large error.

nodes.title: Kepler period
nodes.plain: The relative two-body ellipse has a period determined by semimajor axis and total mass.
conditions: Isolated bound Newtonian two-body system
Ellipse with0<=e<1
derivation: Use angular-momentum conservation and ellipse area.
Insert the inverse-square orbit relation.
limitingCases: Circular limit preserves same period at radiusa
pitfalls: A planet perturbation or relativistic precession violates an exactly closed Kepler ellipse.

nodes.title: Vis-viva relation
nodes.plain: Instantaneous speed follows orbital energy; a is signed for hyperbolic convention.
conditions: Newtonian two-body potential
a>0 for ellipse and a<0 for hyperbola
derivation: Specific energy is-G(M+m)/(2a).
Equate to v²/2-G(M+m)/r.

steps: This is a scaled mathematical example.

limitingCases: a→infinity recovers parabolic escape
pitfalls: Not every numerical r,a pair is consistent with a physical orbit and angular momentum.

nodes.title: Specific mechanical energy
nodes.plain: Energy per unit test mass separates bound, parabolic and unbound Newtonian motion.
conditions: Static point potential
Negligible dissipation
derivation: Divide kinetic plus potential energy by test mass.
Use potential zero at infinity.
limitingCases: epsilon=0 marks parabolic energy
pitfalls: Negative energy does not specify a unique ellipse without angular momentum.

nodes.title: Specific angular momentum
nodes.plain: A central force conserves the orbital plane and areal velocity.
conditions: Central force
No external torque
derivation: Differentiate r×v.
Both v×v and r×radial acceleration vanish.
limitingCases: Pure radial motion has h=0
pitfalls: A nongravitational torque breaks conservation even if gravity remains central.

nodes.title: Point-mass tidal tensor
nodes.plain: Nearby free bodies separate radially and compress transversely in this Newtonian vacuum field.
conditions: Separation much smaller than r
Einstein sum over repeated j
derivation: Linearize g at displaced position.
Differentiate g=-GM r/r³; radial eigenvalue is2GM/r³.
limitingCases: Trace vanishes outside source
pitfalls: A uniform local acceleration can be transformed away; a tidal tensor generally cannot.

nodes.title: Spherical hydrostatic balance

conditions: Spherical static fluid
Newtonian pressure small relative to rest energy density
derivation: Balance pressure force on a thin shell with gravitational force.
Take shell thickness to zero.
limitingCases: Zero density yields zero pressure gradient
pitfalls: Compact stars require relativistic TOV and an equation of state, not this equation.

Collect derivative and quadratic connection terms.

nodes.title: Period and frequency
nodes.plain: Frequency counts repeated cycles per elapsed time; period is the duration of one complete repetition. This definition presupposes a repeatable event and a declared clock, rather than assigning an oscillation to any object by naming it.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: T>0; stationary periodic signal; cycles counted consistently.
derivation: Choose successive equivalent phase crossings.
Divide the number of complete cycles by the elapsed time; for one cycle invert its duration.
limitingCases: As T grows without bound, f approaches zero.
pitfalls: A transient or irregular record need not have one period.

nodes.title: Ordinary versus angular frequency
nodes.plain: A full cycle is 2π radians. Ordinary frequency and angular frequency describe the same periodic evolution with different phase-counting conventions. The radian is a named dimensionless SI unit, but retaining rad in labels prevents factor-of-2π mistakes.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: Sinusoidal phase or a specified phase-rate definition.
derivation: One cycle increments phase by 2π.
Differentiate phase 2πft with respect to time.
limitingCases: Zero frequency gives zero angular frequency.
pitfalls: Do not insert a frequency in Hz into an equation that expects rad/s.

nodes.title: Instantaneous phase frequency
nodes.plain: For a resolved single-component signal, phase slope defines a local frequency. This is conditional on choosing a continuous phase representation and on adequate amplitude and signal quality. It is not a unique decomposition of an arbitrary multicomponent waveform.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
continuous phase under stated unwrap convention

conditions: Unwrapped differentiable phase; amplitude not zero; phase model declared.
derivation: Represent one component by amplitude times cosine of phase.
Define frequency as cycles of phase accumulated per unit time.
limitingCases: Constant phase has zero local frequency.
pitfalls: Phase at an amplitude zero can be undefined; differentiation amplifies noise.

nodes.title: Undamped mass–spring natural frequency
nodes.plain: The free natural frequency follows from stiffness and inertia, not from the current drive. It is the frequency of one selected linearized coordinate under specified constraints. A real body generally supplies many coordinates and modes.
conditions: m>0; K>0; linear Hookean restoring force; no damping.
derivation: Start with m x″+Kx=0.
Insert x=A cos(ωt) and require K−mω²=0.

steps: Divide angular frequency by 2π to express Hz.

limitingCases: K→0 removes the restoring oscillation.
pitfalls: Support stiffness and effective mass must match the same coordinate.

nodes.title: Damped free oscillation
nodes.plain: A viscously damped oscillator rings with an exponential envelope and a shifted oscillation frequency. This describes the underdamped free motion; the frequency of the maximum forced displacement is a different quantity.
conditions: Linear viscous damping; 0≤γ<ω₀.
derivation: Solve the characteristic polynomial r²+2γr+ω₀²=0.
Its roots are −γ±iω_d; the real part sets decay and imaginary part sets oscillation.
limitingCases: At γ=0 recover ω₀; critical damping has no sinusoidal ringing.
pitfalls: Do not continue the square root as a real oscillation above critical damping.
Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation.

nodes.title: Quality factor in the weakly damped oscillator
nodes.plain: Quality factor compares stored energy with energy dissipated over an oscillation. For this linear viscous model the damping definition gives Q=ω₀/(2γ); the familiar energy-lost-per-cycle interpretation is most direct when damping is weak.

variables.meaning: quality factor under the stated energy/linewidth convention

conditions: Positive viscous damping; energy/linewidth comparisons use weak damping.
derivation: The displacement envelope decays as e^(−γt), so energy decays twice as fast.
Compare the energy-loss timescale with the oscillation timescale.
limitingCases: b→0 yields diverging Q in the lossless idealization.
pitfalls: A high Q stores supplied energy; it is not energy creation.
Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation.
Free ring-down amplitude decays at γ while energy decays at 2γ; loaded Q, internal Q and external-coupling Q are not interchangeable.

nodes.title: Complex forced displacement response
nodes.plain: The displacement-to-force transfer function contains both gain and phase. The stated sign follows the e^(iωt) convention. It makes an experimentally useful prediction only when force and displacement channels, units, loading and calibration are specified.

variables.meaning: imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Steady sinusoidal forcing; linear time-invariant system; e^(iωt) phasors.
derivation: Insert complex sinusoidal force and displacement into the equation of motion.
Cancel the common time factor and divide displacement amplitude by force amplitude.

steps: At ω=10 the real stiffness and inertia cancel.

limitingCases: At ω=0 recover static compliance 1/K.
pitfalls: Changing phasor convention conjugates the imaginary sign, not the measurable prediction.

nodes.title: Forced-displacement peak frequency
nodes.plain: For a flat force amplitude and frequency-independent viscous damping, the maximum displacement occurs below the undamped natural frequency. Other measured quantities, such as velocity, absorbed power or a microphone output, can peak elsewhere.
conditions: γ<ω₀/√2; displacement amplitude; constant driving-force amplitude.
derivation: Square the magnitude of the denominator of H.
Set its frequency derivative to zero and select the positive minimum.
limitingCases: At zero damping this approaches ω₀; above the stated bound the interior displacement peak disappears.
pitfalls: A spectral maximum does not automatically equal the isolated object natural mode.
Feynman I23 writes the damping coefficient as b/m; this atlas gamma is b/(2m), requiring an explicit factor-of-two translation.

nodes.title: Loaded resonance linewidth
nodes.plain: The linewidth relationship uses the half-power bandwidth of a single narrow resonance. Loaded Q includes energy loss through the measurement and drive ports as well as internal loss. A different amplitude threshold or a superposition of modes changes the inference.

variables.meaning: quality factor under the stated energy/linewidth convention
centre frequency of the isolated narrow resonance
specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally

conditions: Isolated weakly damped resonance; Δf is full width at half maximum of power.
derivation: Approximate the response denominator near its resonance.
Find the two frequencies where response power is half its peak value.
limitingCases: Vanishing linewidth gives divergent ideal Q.
pitfalls: Half amplitude is not half power; unresolved neighboring peaks violate the fit model.
Δf is the full half-power width, not the half-width-at-half-maximum (HWHM=Δf/2). Loaded loss rates add only when the declared independent-port linear-loss model applies.

nodes.title: Coupled normal-mode eigenproblem
nodes.plain: A coupled body has a family of mode shapes and eigenfrequencies. Positive mass and appropriate stiffness/boundary conditions determine the mathematical problem. A plotted shape alone does not specify the matrices, physical scale or material properties.
conditions: Linear conservative finite-dimensional model; M positive definite; declared supports.
derivation: Insert q(t)=q₀e^(iωt) into Mq″+Kq=0.
Require a nonzero eigenvector instead of inverting a singular dynamic stiffness.
limitingCases: A zero stiffness eigenvalue is a rigid or marginal mode, not a positive resonance.
pitfalls: Degeneracies and damping can require different modal coordinates.

nodes.title: Nondispersive wave equation
nodes.plain: For a uniform one-dimensional nondispersive medium, sinusoidal plane waves satisfy a linear relation between angular frequency and spatial wave number. The medium speed belongs to that wave equation and is not automatically the vacuum speed of light.

variables.meaning: phase speed in the declared medium

conditions: Linear uniform 1D medium; no dispersion, dissipation or unspecified boundaries.
derivation: Insert u=A exp(i(kx−ωt)).
Cancel the nonzero wave factor and compare ω² with c²k².
limitingCases: At k=0 the chosen acoustic branch has ω=0.
pitfalls: A boundary-value spectrum needs boundary conditions beyond a plane-wave dispersion law.

nodes.title: Phase and group velocity
nodes.plain: Phase speed follows constant phase; group speed follows the envelope of a narrow wave packet under suitable smooth dispersion. Neither expression alone proves a signal-front speed or licenses superluminal information transfer.
conditions: k≠0 for phase speed; smooth branch and narrowband packet for group speed.
derivation: Keep kx−ωt constant for a phase crest.
Expand ω(k) to first order around the carrier to obtain envelope translation.
limitingCases: For ω=ck both reduce to c.
pitfalls: Absorbing and strongly distorted pulses need more than an envelope-velocity formula.

nodes.title: Fixed-end string modes
nodes.plain: A string fixed at both ends supports integer spatial half-wavelengths. This is a declared string model, not a formula that assigns a monument, sigil or arbitrary image its natural frequency.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
integer mode or comb index under the local definition
phase speed in the declared medium

conditions: Uniform ideal string; fixed displacement at both ends; n positive integer.
derivation: Boundary zeros require k_nL=nπ.
Combine ω=ck with f=ω/(2π).
limitingCases: Double L at fixed c and n to halve f.
pitfalls: Air cavities and elastic plates have different boundary equations.

nodes.title: Ideal rigid rectangular-room modes
nodes.plain: A separable pressure-wave model in a rigid rectangular cavity gives a modal family indexed by three nonnegative integers. Wall impedance, openings, obstacles and real geometry change this spectrum and its linewidths.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
phase speed in the declared medium
nonnegative integer mode index along x
nonnegative integer mode index along y
nonnegative integer mode index along z

conditions: Rigid-wall pressure Neumann boundaries; rectangular uniform medium; indices not all zero.
derivation: Separate the Helmholtz equation into three cosine factors.
Add the squared axial wave numbers and convert angular frequency to Hz.

steps: Only the 5 m axial term remains.

limitingCases: Scale every room dimension by two to halve every mode frequency.
pitfalls: L_x,L_y,L_z each have units m; n_x,n_y,n_z are integer indices. A photograph does not supply these dimensions or walls.

nodes.title: Continuous Fourier transform convention
nodes.plain: The transform resolves a time signal into complex frequency components under one explicit normalization. Displacement data produce transform units of metre-seconds. Generalized functions are needed for ideal infinite-duration pure tones.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Integrable signal or stated generalized-function/L2 interpretation.
derivation: Project the signal onto complex exponentials with frequency f.
Retain the dt factor, which supplies the time dimension.

inputs.signal: x(t)=e^(−at) for t≥0; a=2 s⁻¹, amplitude1 m

limitingCases: At f=0 the transform equals the time integral of the signal.
pitfalls: An FFT array is not automatically the continuous transform without sample-spacing scaling.

nodes.title: Inverse Fourier reconstruction
nodes.plain: Under compatible hypotheses the inverse combines complex components to recover the signal. The frequency integral supplies inverse seconds, restoring the original signal units; phase is essential to the reconstruction.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Sufficient pointwise form: x and its Fourier transform X are both integrable on R; the inverse equals x almost everywhere and at continuity points. L2 inversion is a separate mean-square statement.
derivation: Use orthogonality in the distributional or Hilbert-space sense.
Integrate X against the opposite-sign exponential.

steps: Apply the inverse with its specified sign.
workedExample.result: Recover the causal exponential at continuity points.

limitingCases: Removing all Fourier components gives the zero signal.
pitfalls: Magnitude-only spectra generally cannot reconstruct phase or a unique time waveform.

nodes.title: Linear convolution theorem
nodes.plain: For a linear time-invariant channel, convolution in time corresponds to multiplication in frequency. The output spectrum includes the channel response, so a strong output line can come from propagation, sensor or electronics rather than the source alone.

variables.meaning: input signal, here displacement for unit illustration
convolution: (h*x)(t)=∫h(t−u)x(u)du, where u and t are time coordinates in seconds
variables.unit: operator convention; includes integration over s
maps a signal unit to signal unit·s

variables.meaning: Fourier transform of the impulse response

conditions: Sufficient classical form: x,h are integrable on R, so Fubini applies; compatible Fourier convention. A physical time-domain impulse kernel has output/(input·s) units and its H has output/input units.
derivation: Insert the convolution integral into the Fourier definition.
Exchange integrals under appropriate convergence conditions and shift the time variable.
limitingCases: H=0 suppresses every source component at that frequency.
pitfalls: A transfer-function zero destroys information that naive division cannot restore.

nodes.title: Causal Laplace transform and convergence
nodes.plain: The Laplace variable carries both decay/growth weighting and angular oscillation. Its region of convergence is part of the transform. A formal substitution s=iω does not establish that a Fourier transform exists on that boundary.

variables.meaning: causal Laplace transform of displacement x(t)
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Causal convention; integral converges for stated Re(s).
derivation: Multiply the causal response by exponential weighting.
Identify where the tail integral converges before simplifying algebra.
limitingCases: At s=0 recover total area 0.5 m·s.
pitfalls: The algebraic fraction alone omits the causal region of convergence.

nodes.title: Finite discrete Fourier transform
nodes.plain: The DFT is an exact invertible change of coordinates for a finite sample vector under its chosen normalization. It is not, by itself, proof of the spectrum of the unsampled physical world.

variables.meaning: sampled signal, here displacement for unit illustration
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: N positive integer; forward transform unscaled, inverse divided by N.
derivation: Choose the N orthogonal discrete complex exponentials.
Compute their finite inner products with the sample vector.
limitingCases: A constant vector has only its DC coefficient nonzero.
pitfalls: FFT names an algorithm; DFT names the mathematical transform.

nodes.title: DFT frequency grid
nodes.plain: The standard DFT grid spacing is reciprocal record duration. Zero padding provides additional interpolation points but does not create an independently longer measurement or separate arbitrarily close noisy components.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally

conditions: Uniform sampling; T_obs=N/f_s; signed negative bins identified consistently.
derivation: N equally spaced phase patterns span the finite vector.
Convert phase advance per sample into cycles per second.
limitingCases: Doubling observation duration at fixed rate halves grid spacing.
pitfalls: Grid spacing, estimator uncertainty and two-line resolution are different notions.

nodes.title: Discrete-time alias equivalence
nodes.plain: Sampling identifies complex tones whose frequencies differ by an integer sampling rate. Real cosines add sign ambiguity. No later plot or machine-learning method can distinguish those aliases from the identical samples without additional assumptions or measurements.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
integer mode or comb index under the local definition
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Uniform ideal sample times; n and j integers.
derivation: Expand the extra phase as 2πnj.
Its complex exponential equals one for every sample.

steps: Their difference is one sampling rate.

limitingCases: Adding n=0 leaves the same frequency.
pitfalls: Anti-alias filtering must occur before irrecoverable sampling.

nodes.title: Bandlimited sampling condition
nodes.plain: A strictly bandlimited signal can be reconstructed in the ideal sampling theorem when the sample rate exceeds twice its highest frequency. Equality is delicate: a sine exactly at Nyquist can vanish at every sample. Real hardware needs a transition band and analog filtering.

variables.meaning: highest absolute occupied signal frequency B, not an arbitrary oscillator carrier
bandlimit used in the stated theorem hypothesis; equal to f_max

conditions: Ideal theorem: an L2 continuous-time signal has Fourier support in [−B,B] with B<f_s/2; infinitely many exact uniform samples and the associated ideal reconstruction are available. A finite record and real filter need extra error analysis.
derivation: Sampling repeats the spectrum every f_s.
Require its shifted copies not to overlap.

workedExample.result: A 4000 Hz zero-phase sine samples to zero; 1000 Hz is within the strict band.

limitingCases: DC remains representable if the measurement chain preserves it.
pitfalls: A high sample rate alone does not certify bandwidth, clock accuracy or sensor calibration.

nodes.title: Periodic Hann analysis window
nodes.plain: Windowing reduces discontinuities in the assumed repeated record, trading spectral leakage against main-lobe width and changing amplitude normalization. The periodic N-denominator form differs from the symmetric N−1 form used in some applications.
conditions: N>1; explicitly periodic window for DFT analysis.
derivation: Combine a constant with one cosine over the record.
Multiplication in time convolves spectra and changes apparent peak shape.
limitingCases: A rectangular window is the distinct choice w_j=1.
pitfalls: Do not mix symmetric and periodic window calibration constants.

nodes.title: Coherent window gain
nodes.plain: The mean window weight calibrates a bin-centred coherent tone under the declared transform convention. It is not the same normalization used for broadband noise power, which depends on the sum of squared weights.
conditions: Coherent bin-centred tone; nonzero sum of window values; corresponding amplitude estimator.
derivation: Window a coherent complex tone and evaluate its matching DFT bin.
All phase terms cancel, leaving the sum of window weights.
limitingCases: A rectangular window gives G=1.
pitfalls: For real tone amplitude, also account for the positive/negative-frequency split and DC/Nyquist exceptions.

nodes.title: Two-sided windowed periodogram density
nodes.plain: Power spectral density records signal squared per hertz, rather than signal amplitude or a per-bin power. A one-sided real-data form doubles the positive interior bins, retaining separate DC and Nyquist treatment.

variables.meaning: sampled signal, here displacement for unit illustration

conditions: Real or complex finite samples; detrending and two-sided convention stated; nonzero window energy.
For real data, one-sided interior positive-frequency bins are doubled. DC is not doubled; for even N the Nyquist bin is not doubled; for odd N there is no Nyquist endpoint bin.
derivation: Square the windowed transform magnitude.
Normalize by sample rate and total window-squared weight for density units.

workedExample.result: PSD unit is V²/Hz; an integrated band has V².

limitingCases: Zero samples produce zero PSD.
pitfalls: A log plot must state its reference and whether it displays amplitude, power or density.

nodes.title: DFT energy identity
nodes.plain: Parseval’s finite identity checks normalization by matching the squared norm in sample and DFT coordinates. It is a mathematical identity for this vector; converting it to physical energy still requires sample spacing, impedances and a calibrated channel model.

variables.meaning: sampled signal, here displacement for unit illustration

conditions: Unscaled forward DFT and 1/N inverse; finite vector.
derivation: Use discrete exponential orthogonality.
Cross terms vanish except matching sample indices.
limitingCases: The zero vector gives zero on both sides.
pitfalls: Sum of microphone-pressure squared is not automatically joules.

nodes.title: Short-time Fourier transform
nodes.plain: The STFT measures local spectral content under a chosen window and hop. It shows change across the record but trades temporal localization against frequency discrimination. A bright ridge is conditional on this representation and its calibration.

variables.meaning: dimensionless continuous analysis window translated to τ
window centre or averaging time as declared locally
ordinary frequency in cycles per second
imaginary unit satisfying i²=−1; not electric current

conditions: Specified window, overlap/hop, padding, normalization and sampling.
derivation: Multiply by a translated window.
Transform that local weighted segment and repeat across centre times.

steps: Its basic frequency grid is 10 Hz before padding.

limitingCases: A window covering the full record reduces to one windowed transform.
pitfalls: A smaller hop does not independently improve the window’s frequency resolution.

nodes.title: L2-normalized continuous wavelet transform
nodes.plain: Wavelet scale stretches a declared mother wavelet. Scale is not automatically hertz; converting it to frequency depends on the wavelet’s centre-frequency convention and sample period. Small sampled scales may alias even when the original input was properly sampled.

variables.meaning: continuous wavelet coefficient for L2-normalized scale
window centre or averaging time as declared locally

conditions: a>0; admissible suitable mother wavelet; dimensional scale in seconds here.
derivation: Translate the analysing wavelet in time.
Stretch it by a and normalize its L2 norm before taking the signal inner product.

steps: For this declared centre, divide one cycle by 0.01 s.

limitingCases: Different mother-wavelet centres give different scale-to-Hz mappings.
pitfalls: Software scales may be dimensionless sample counts; do not reuse a seconds-based formula without conversion.

nodes.title: Floquet factorization of periodic linear dynamics
nodes.plain: A periodic linear differential equation admits a fundamental-matrix factorization under standard continuity conditions. The eigenvalues of its constant generator describe growth and phase modulo a drive-frequency convention. This is not a general claim that all periodically driven matter has a single frequency.

variables.meaning: fundamental matrix of linear periodic dynamics

conditions: Finite-dimensional complex linear system u′=A(t)u with continuous A(t+T)=A(t), T>0; normalized invertible fundamental matrix U(0)=I; a complex logarithm of its nonsingular monodromy is chosen.
derivation: Propagate over one drive period to form the monodromy matrix.
Choose a matrix logarithm and remove its exponential evolution to leave a periodic factor.

inputs.equation: x′=iωx; coefficients are constant and hence T-periodic

workedExample.result: U=e^(iωt); quasifrequency is defined modulo 2π/T under branch changes.

limitingCases: With zero drive the autonomous solution remains included.
pitfalls: A branch of a logarithm and stability/observable definitions must be declared.

nodes.title: Optical frequency-comb tooth relation
nodes.plain: A stabilized comb links an integer sequence of optical modes to repetition and carrier-envelope-offset frequencies. Its utility requires mode-number identification, controlled offsets and a calibrated reference; the formula alone is not an accurate clock or range measurement.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second
integer mode or comb index under the local definition

conditions: Comb regime with identifiable mode index and defined offset/repetition references.
derivation: A pulse train supplies equally spaced Fourier components.
Pulse-to-pulse carrier-envelope slip offsets the entire tooth grid.

steps: Multiply mode number by repetition rate and add offset.

limitingCases: f_CEO=0 yields an integer repetition-rate grid.
pitfalls: An incorrect tooth number creates an enormous systematic error despite a narrow beat note.

nodes.title: Two-tone beating identity
nodes.plain: A pair of monaural tones has a rapid carrier factor and a slowly varying signed factor. The magnitude envelope repeats at the absolute tone separation. This algebra does not model dichotic binaural perception, EEG entrainment or clinical outcomes.

variables.meaning: specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally

conditions: f_c=(f₁+f₂)/2; Δf=f₂−f₁; equal phases/amplitudes in this identity.
derivation: Apply the sine-sum identity.
Keep carrier frequency and tone separation as distinct observables.

steps: Compute centre 224 Hz and separation 8 Hz.
workedExample.result: Signed envelope cos(8πt); magnitude envelope repeats at 8 Hz.

limitingCases: Equal tones give an unmodulated tone of double amplitude.
pitfalls: The signed cosine factor has frequency |Δf|/2; its absolute envelope has repetition rate |Δf|.

nodes.title: Vacuum electromagnetic wavelength
nodes.plain: Frequency converts to wavelength through the propagation law of the declared channel. The exact vacuum speed applies to electromagnetic waves in vacuum. Acoustic frequency needs a sound speed, while a material dispersion relation can make phase and group wavelengths more complicated.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: Vacuum electromagnetic plane wave; f>0.
derivation: Use one-period propagation distance.
Set λ=c₀T and invert T.
limitingCases: At fixed speed, doubling frequency halves wavelength.
pitfalls: Do not use c₀/f for a sound wave in air or a body vibration.

nodes.title: Quantum transition and photon energy
nodes.plain: A photon or an energy gap associated with a resonant quantum transition relates energy to temporal frequency through Planck’s constant. This does not identify the total energy of a classical acoustic wave from its frequency alone; occupation and amplitude also matter.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: Photon energy or specified quantum transition; not arbitrary classical total energy.
derivation: Combine Planck’s relation with ω=2πf and ℏ=h/(2π).
Check that J·s multiplied by s⁻¹ gives joules.
limitingCases: Zero frequency gives zero photon energy in this relation, not a nontrivial static photon oscillator.
pitfalls: A classical oscillator has many energy levels/occupations; a high frequency alone is not a high total stored energy.

nodes.title: Lorentzian field-coherence linewidth relation
nodes.plain: For a stationary exponentially decaying first-order field correlation, the spectrum is Lorentzian and its full-width-at-half-maximum is reciprocal π times the field-correlation time. Other line shapes or intensity-correlation definitions give different relations.

variables.meaning: specified bandwidth or tone separation, as defined locally
first-order field-correlation decay time for declared Lorentzian line

conditions: First-order field correlation proportional to exp(−|t|/τ_c); Lorentzian power spectrum.
derivation: Fourier-transform the two-sided exponential correlation.
Solve where the resulting Lorentzian is half its zero-offset value.
limitingCases: Longer field coherence narrows the Lorentzian.
pitfalls: Do not substitute an intensity lifetime without checking the factor of two and correlation definition.

nodes.title: Fractional frequency deviation
nodes.plain: Fractional frequency compares an oscillator to a specified nominal/reference frequency. It is dimensionless and makes clock comparisons across very different carrier frequencies meaningful, while leaving reference calibration and correlations explicit.
conditions: ν₀>0; common time coordinate and declared reference.
derivation: Subtract nominal frequency from observed frequency.
Normalize by the declared nominal value.
limitingCases: Zero frequency offset yields y=0.
pitfalls: An unstable or drifting reference contributes to the observed difference.

nodes.title: Non-overlapping Allan variance estimator
nodes.plain: Allan variance measures changes between adjacent averages rather than deviation from one global mean. The averaging time and noise class are essential. A stability statistic is not by itself a full systematic-uncertainty or accuracy evaluation.

variables.meaning: Allan deviation at averaging time τ
window centre or averaging time as declared locally
mean fractional frequency in interval i of duration τ

conditions: M≥2 adjacent non-overlapping interval averages of length τ; gaps/dead time and drift treatment stated.
derivation: Compute adjacent averaged-frequency differences.
Average their squares and divide by two.
limitingCases: A constant fractional offset has zero Allan variance.
pitfalls: That constant offset may still make the clock inaccurate; zero variance does not mean correct time.

nodes.title: White-frequency averaging benchmark
nodes.plain: For white frequency noise and an appropriate measurement process, Allan deviation improves as averaging time to the minus one-half power. Drift, flicker floors, dead time and correlated noise prevent extrapolating this law indefinitely.

variables.meaning: Allan deviation at averaging time τ
white-frequency Allan deviation at τ=1 s
window centre or averaging time as declared locally

conditions: White frequency noise in the assessed averaging range; σ₁ refers to 1 s.
derivation: Average independent fluctuations over more samples.
Their variance falls inversely with averaging duration, so deviation falls as its square root.
limitingCases: At τ=1 s recover σ₁.
pitfalls: A plotted slope alone does not prove the underlying noise is white at unmeasured times.

nodes.title: Weak-field gravitational clock shift
nodes.plain: Two otherwise comparable clocks at different gravitational potentials accumulate different proper times. Near Earth in a small static height interval, the higher clock runs faster by approximately gΔh/c₀². This is a conditional relativistic comparison, not motion changing an object’s intrinsic material constant.

variables.meaning: height difference under weak static-field approximation

conditions: Weak static field; small local vertical interval; potential difference≈gΔh; kinematic terms separately assessed.
derivation: Expand the proper-time ratio to first order in gravitational potential difference/c₀².
Approximate the local potential difference by gΔh.
limitingCases: Equal potential gives zero gravitational differential under these assumptions.
pitfalls: Height must be tied to a geopotential model for precision work; velocity effects are separate.

nodes.title: Nuclear-scale optical frequency conversion
nodes.plain: The unusually low-energy thorium-229 transition lies in the vacuum-ultraviolet optical range even though the participating states are nuclear. The word nuclear therefore does not by itself specify a gamma-ray frequency, clock performance or a deployed time standard.

variables.meaning: ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: An independently measured/assumed transition energy; illustrative value, not a claim of a new precision determination.
derivation: Convert electronvolts to joules using the exact elementary charge.
Divide transition energy by Planck’s constant.
limitingCases: Changing the assumed energy changes frequency proportionally.
pitfalls: 8.4 eV is a rounded illustration, not the quoted precision of a particular paper.

nodes.title: First-order uncertainty propagation with covariance
nodes.plain: A differentiable map carries input covariance into output covariance through its Jacobian. Correlations can cancel or amplify uncertainty in ratios. This linearization must be checked when distributions, nonlinearity or denominator uncertainty are substantial.

variables.meaning: Jacobian of derived quantities with respect to inputs

conditions: Differentiable map near the estimate; small uncertainties; covariance and units declared.
derivation: Linearize the map as δy≈Jδx.
Take the covariance expectation while retaining cross terms.
limitingCases: Perfect common-mode correlation cancels the difference uncertainty in this ideal case.
pitfalls: Independent-error quadrature is wrong when the two channels share a reference.

nodes.title: Source–channel–receiver measurement model
nodes.plain: A measured spectrum combines the source, propagation/instrument transfer and additive noise. Multiple source/channel pairs can produce the same record. A peak or a learned embedding is therefore not a unique reconstruction of source physics without calibration and constraints.

variables.meaning: Fourier transform of additive measurement noise η(t); not sample-count N
ordinary frequency in cycles per second

conditions: Frequency-domain linear channel within declared bandwidth; noise convention and units stated.
derivation: Model the instrument response as convolution plus additive noise.
Transform under the compatible Fourier convention.

steps: Both pairs give the same output component 6.
workedExample.result: Output alone cannot distinguish these source/channel amplitudes.

limitingCases: At H=0 source components are unobservable through this channel.
pitfalls: Noise is N(f), the transform of η(t), not the sample-count N used in the DFT.

nodes.title: Rectangular interrogation power linewidth
nodes.plain: A finite rectangular coherent interrogation produces a sinc-squared power/excitation profile. Its width comes from interaction duration and is not an intrinsic Lorentzian lifetime.

variables.meaning: unnormalized sinc sin(u)/u, with continuous value1 at u=0
full width between the two half-power points

conditions: Constant-amplitude rectangular coherent time window. Power is squared Fourier amplitude; strong-drive Rabi/dephasing/loss effects may require the full excitation model.
derivation: Integrate a complex exponential over a centred interval of durationT to obtain T sin(πΔfT)/(πΔfT).
Normalize and square the amplitude; solve(sin u/u)^2=1/2 for u≈1.391557, then take the full two-sided detuning width2u/(πT).

workedExample.result: about1.18119Hz, close to the reported1.2Hz source spectrum; not an independent experimental fit

limitingCases: T→∞ narrows the ideal central lobe; a nonrectangular or incoherent interaction changes the profile.
pitfalls: sinc here is sin(u)/u, not the normalized software sinc sin(πu)/(πu).
Do not insert this FWHM into the Lorentzian field-coherence formula1/(πτ_c).

nodes.title: Scalar Gaussian forward-KL risk
nodes.plain: The expected predictive log-loss penalty for estimating an unknown Gaussian variance has a finite closed form only above its inverse-moment threshold.

variables.meaning: expected forward Kullback–Leibler divergence in nats

conditions: True observations IID N(0,v*),v*>0; mean known.
MLE uses divisor n; forward direction true distribution to fitted distribution; n>2.
derivation: Write X=n vhat/v* as chi-square(n).
Use KL=.5[log(vhat/v*)+v*/vhat−1].
E logX=ψ(n/2)+log2 and E(1/X)=1/(n−2).
limitingCases: n≤2 gives infinite forward risk.
E_n→0 as n→∞ under correct specification.
pitfalls: Reverse KL is a different expectation.
A two-point calculation illustrates but does not prove all-n monotonicity.

nodes.title: Finite benchmark scoring convention
nodes.plain: The reported count applies a threshold to averaged referee scores, not a trusted-kernel decision.
conditions: Use First ProofBatch3 rubric and ten tasks.
Missing submissions countzero; threshold.5.
derivation: Read each mean grade inTable2.
Apply≥.5 and sum indicators.
limitingCases: All abstentions producezero.
A score.5 is counted despite incomplete confidence.
pitfalls: Do not read3/10 as three fully machine-certified proofs.
These tasks are not a random sample of all mathematics.
Under the stricter mean-grade-equals1 convention, Siege has2/10; that alternate count is not the report’s published total.

nodes.title: Permanent definition
nodes.plain: Sum one product per permutation, without determinant signs.

variables.meaning: square matrix over a commutative field

conditions: Square n×n matrix; a commutative coefficient field.
derivation: Each permutation chooses one entry from every row and column.
All chosen products are added with coefficient+1.
limitingCases: For1×1, permanent equals its entry.
Diagonal matrices give the product of diagonal entries.
pitfalls: Definition does not establish any claimed circuit lower bound.
Arithmetic model and coefficient field matter for complexity.

nodes.title: ε-light set definition
nodes.plain: Every quadratic energy of induced edges is bounded by ε times the original graph energy.
conditions: Finite undirected graph and compatible nonnegative edge weights.
PSD order refers to all real vectors, not entrywise inequalities.
derivation: Laplacian energy is sum over edges of w_uv(z_u−z_v)².
Subtract induced-edge energy from ε times total.

steps: Induced graph has no edges, soL_S=0.
workedExample.result: SingletonS is ε-light; both vertices are not forε<1.

limitingCases: EmptyS always passes.
Atε=1, allV passes.
pitfalls: Checking one test vector is insufficient.
This example does not prove the universal large-subset theorem.

nodes.title: For IID N(0,Σ*) samples in dimensiond, Σ*>0, prove expected forward KL risk of covariance MLE strictly decreases for n>d+1, and is infinite for n≤d+1; paper extends to unknown mean and other families.

nodes.problemStatement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers o; let N_r be the upper-triangular unipotent subgroup of GL_r(F). Fix a nontrivial additive character ψ of conductor o and a generic irreducible admissible representation Π of GL_(n+1)(F) in W(Π,ψ^(-1)). Must there exist one W in that Whittaker model such that, for every generic irreducible admissible π of GL_n(F) in W(π,ψ), with conductor idealq, generatorQ of q^(-1), and u_Q=I_(n+1)+Q E_(n,n+1), some V∈W(π,ψ) makes ∫_(N_n\GL_n(F)) W(diag(g,1)u_Q)V(g)|det g|^(s−1/2)dg finite and nonzero for every s∈C?
nodes.priorStatus: A hidden-solution research benchmark question, not evidence that all relevant theory was globally unsolved.
nodes.AIContribution: Internal model generated/typeset attempt; humans selected attempts and requested clarification based on feedback.
nodes.verificationStatus: Provider explicitly corrected its initial likely-correct assessment to incorrect.
nodes.independentEvidence: OpenAI cites organizer commentary and community analysis; selected organizer text inspected, not an independent re-derivation of this attempt.
nodes.limitations: The order of quantifiers matters: one W is selected before varying π; V may depend on π. The representation-theoretic setup is reproduced from organizer Problem2. This record audits an explicitly corrected attempt, not a solved theorem.
nodes.title: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers o; let N_r be the upper-triangular unipotent subgroup of GL_r(F). Fix a nontrivial additive character ψ of conductor o and a generic irreducible admissible representation Π of GL_(n+1)(F) in W(Π,ψ^(-1)). nodes.problemStatement: For monic real-rooted degree-n polynomials p,q with the organizer’s finite free additive convolution, is 1/Φ_n(p⊞_n q)≥1/Φ_n(p)+1/Φ_n(q), with Φ_n(p)=Σ_{i≤n}Σ_{j≠i}(1/(λ_i−λ_j))² and Φ=∞ at repeated roots?
nodes.priorStatus: Research-level hidden-solution challenge; prior human solutions existed.
nodes.AIContribution: Model-generated proof attempt, human best-of selection and clarification.
nodes.verificationStatus: Company reports high chance of correctness, not a machine-checked theorem verdict.
nodes.independentEvidence: Organizer provides exact statement; its early GPT-5.2 baseline comments do not grade this later internal-model attempt.
nodes.limitations: Polynomial normalization and repeated-root conventions matter; complete proof not independently audited. The Φ definition is transcribed as the source’s double sum of squared reciprocals.
nodes.title: For monic real-rooted degree-n polynomials p,q with the organizer’s finite free additive convolution, is 1/Φ_n(p⊞_n q)≥1/Φ_n(p)+1/Φ_n(q), with Φ_n(p)=Σ_{i≤n}Σ_{j≠i}(1/(λ_i−λ_j))² and Φ=∞ at repeated roots?

nodes.problemStatement: Does a universal c>0 exist such that every finite graph and 0<ε<1 admit S⊂V with |S|≥cε|V| and L_S≼εL, where L_S retains only edges insideS?
nodes.priorStatus: Hidden human-solved spectral graph question in First Proof.
nodes.AIContribution: Generated proof with limited human supervision and expert-feedback clarification.
nodes.verificationStatus: Provider provisional high-confidence result.
nodes.independentEvidence: Organizer statement inspected; no independent verification of this exact internal attempt obtained.
nodes.limitations: A sampled graph experiment cannot prove the universal existence claim; PSD means positive-semidefinite order.
nodes.title: Does a universal c>0 exist such that every finite graph and 0<ε<1 admit S⊂V with |S|≥cε|V| and L_S≼εL, where L_S retains only edges insideS?

nodes.problemStatement: For n≥5 and Zariski-generic A^(α)∈R^(3×4), find n-independent-degree polynomial relations recognizing exactly the coordinatewise tensor scalings λ_αβγδ=u_αv_βw_γx_δ of determinant tensors, with the organizer’s nonzero-pattern restriction.
nodes.priorStatus: Hidden-solution algebraic research challenge.
nodes.AIContribution: Generated candidate argument; humans selected and formatted outputs.
nodes.verificationStatus: Provider high-chance assessment; proof not independently checked here.
nodes.independentEvidence: Exact organizer problem and internal submitted section9 retrieved.
nodes.limitations: Genericity, exceptional index pattern and if-and-only-if direction must survive formalization; omitted zero cases can change the question.
nodes.title: For n≥5 and Zariski-generic A^(α)∈R^(3×4), find n-independent-degree polynomial relations recognizing exactly the coordinatewise tensor scalings λ_αβγδ=u_αv_βw_γx_δ of determinant tensors, with the organizer’s nonzero-pattern restriction.

nodes.AIContribution: Provider says model generated argument; humans/model prepared manuscript and Lean certificate.

nodes.independentEvidence: No claim-specific independent correctness verdict located; code existence and MathHelm’s broad response are different evidence types.
nodes.limitations: Do not label accepted solely from provider formalization claim; exact theorem/imports/axioms need pinned build and comparison.
nodes.title: For k-colour triangle Ramsey numberR_k(3), claim logR_k(3)=Θ(k logk), hence R_k(3)^(1/k)→∞; reported as resolving Erdős183.

nodes.AIContribution: Generated proof, human-assisted manuscript preparation, claimed Lean formalization.
nodes.verificationStatus: Announcement and manuscript abstract read; proof module/build not audited.
nodes.independentEvidence: No independent claim-specific proof review captured.
nodes.limitations: Convex-body hypotheses and lattice normalization are essential; graph node is a documented claim, not certified resolution.
nodes.title: Claim vol(K)≤(n+1)^n/n! for convex bodies K⊂R^n whose centroid is the unique interior lattice point, in the stated lattice-volume convention.

nodes.title: Claim division-free arithmetic circuit lower boundΩ(n²loglogn) and arithmetic-formula leaf lower boundΩ(n⁴/logn) for the n×n permanent under the manuscript’s algebraic model.

nodes.AIContribution: Model-generated construction; manuscript/certificate prepared with human involvement.

nodes.limitations: Existence of a Lean filename is not evidence the mathematical statement matches the historical question.
nodes.title: Claim an explicit countable group which is not sofic, disproving that every countable group admits the required finite permutation approximations.

nodes.title: Three manuscripts on split abelian eightfold Weil classes, Kuga–Satake correspondences for K3 surfaces, and rational Hodge for products of K3 surfaces were withdrawn after a sign-error-dependent construction failed.
